API Documentation

A REST + WebSocket API for real-time sports data. Every success is JSON with a { data, meta? } envelope; errors return a real HTTP status with { error: { code, message } }. Every id is our own stable id. Every team, league and player carries an image: an absolute URL on https://cdn.sportsapi.app, or null when it has none. The full contract — every field, unit and enum value — is in the reference and in /v2/openapi.json (OpenAPI 3.1, no key needed).

2026-10-28: Monthly request quotas on paid plans — a breaking change (WebSocket protocol 4). See the changelog for every change, before and after.
Base URLhttps://api.sportsapi.app
AuthenticationAuthorization: Bearer sk_live_…
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" \
    https://api.sportsapi.app/v2/livescores?sport=football
Try any endpoint with your own key, no code, in the dashboard Playground.Open Playground

Every /v2request needs an API key. Create one in the dashboard. Keys are shown once at creation; revoke and replace a leaked key there (a revoked key stops working at once). An account holds at most 10 active keys, and all of them share the account's rate limit and quota. CORS is open, but never ship a key in a public web page: anyone can read it.

Sign-up and log-in are throttled: 5 sign-ups per IP per hour, 30 log-in attempts per IP and 10 per email per 10 minutes. Over that they answer 429 rate_limited with Retry-After.

Rate limits & plans

Two independent limits apply to every authenticated /v2 call, per account (shared by all its keys — more keys do not raise them):

  • Quota: requests per UTC calendar month on Starter, Pro and Business (resetting at 00:00 UTC on the 1st), per UTC day on Free (resetting at 00:00 UTC). Every response carries RateLimit-Limit (the quota), RateLimit-Remaining (requests left in it) and RateLimit-Reset (seconds until it resets). Going over returns 429 quota_exceeded with Retry-After set to the seconds until the reset.
  • Rate: requests per minute, in fixed one-minute windows (burst protection; the figures are in the plan table below). It has no headers of its own: going over returns 429 rate_limited with Retry-After (seconds until the next minute) and does not count against the quota.

Ticket requests count like any other call. Requests rejected with 401 or 403 endpoint_not_in_plan are not counted. Every plan gets every sport and every data endpoint but two; plans differ in volume, rate, history depth and WebSocket grade, and the win-probability model (/v2/fixtures/{id}/win-probability) and AI commentary (/v2/fixtures/{id}/commentary) are Pro and Business only.

History: a plan reaches back a set number of days from the start of today (UTC). A fixture that kicked off earlier, a day list of an earlier date, and a league season that ended earlier (standings, rounds, top players and teams, team and player season statistics) answer 403 history_not_in_plan, with historyFrom— the first day you can read — in the error. Fixture lists (a team's or player's fixtures, a round) leave the older fixtures out and say so in meta.historyFrom. Upcoming and live data are never limited. These refusals count against the quota like any other call.

PlanQuotaRequests / minHistoryWebSocketWin probability & AI commentary
Free100 / day10Last 7 days——
Starter750,000 / month300Last 3 months——
Pro4,500,000 / month600Last 12 months—Yes
Business90,000,000 / month6,000Full historyFull · replayYes

Errors

Errors return a real HTTP status and { error: { code, message } }. Branch on error.code, never on the message text.

HTTP/1.1 404
{ "error": { "code": "not_found", "message": "resource not found" } }
StatusCodeMeaning
400bad_requestinvalid id, unknown sport, missing or invalid date, season, round or query, invalid type or page (the message names the allowed values)
400captcha_invalidPOST /contact, POST /auth/login: the captcha is missing, wrong, expired or used — fetch a new one (GET /captcha)
400captcha_requiredPOST /auth/login after 3 failed attempts: send captchaId + captchaAnswer
401unauthorizedmissing, invalid or revoked API key (dashboard API: no valid session token)
401session_revokeddashboard API only: the session was ended by “sign out everywhere” — sign in again
401account_suspendeddashboard API only: the account is suspended
403ws_not_availablestream ticket requested on a plan without WebSocket access
403endpoint_not_in_planthe endpoint is outside your key’s plan: win probability and AI commentary on Free and Starter, and the public demo key outside its few endpoints
403history_not_in_planthe fixture, race, day or season is older than your plan’s history (Free 7 days, Starter 3 months, Pro 12 months, Business no limit); historyFrom in the error is the first day you can read
404not_foundno such resource (an id we never issued, an unknown ranking type, a session or season of another race or series, or a route that does not exist)
404no_datathe ids are ours but the source has no such data: standings, team / player season statistics, the player-statistics explorer, a league’s or series’ seasons (since 2026-10-23; not_found before)
404not_supportedwin probability or AI commentary of a fixture that is not football; the player-statistics explorer of a league that is not football
410password_signup_closedPOST /auth/signup only: new accounts come from Google / GitHub sign-in
429rate_limitedper-minute rate exceeded — wait Retry-After seconds
429quota_exceededrequest quota used up — per UTC month on Starter, Pro and Business (resets 00:00 UTC on the 1st), per UTC day on Free (resets 00:00 UTC); the message names the period and the reset time, Retry-After gives the seconds until the reset
500internal_errorour fault; safe to retry (the message is always generic)
503upstream_unavailabledata temporarily unavailable; retry after the Retry-After seconds (503 since 2026-10-27 — it was 502, which Cloudflare replaced with its own page, so the JSON never arrived)

Data freshness

Responses are served from our store and refreshed from the source as they age. The live state of a match — status, score, clock, winner — comes from the source’s live feed and is current to the second in every response that carries the fixture. How old the rest can be while the data is changing, at worst, with the source healthy (during a source outage we keep serving the last copy we have rather than an error):

EndpointHow current
WebSocket, /v2/livescores, /v2/sportsReal time: pushed from the source’s live feed within seconds. Esports period scores (League of Legends kills per game), which the feed sends only every few minutes, within about 15 seconds while the fixture has a fixture:{id} subscriber.
Status, score, clock and winner of a fixture in play or just finished — wherever a Fixture appearsSeconds. Every response that embeds fixtures (fixture detail, livescores by sport, fixtures by date, team / player / round fixtures) is brought up to the live feed when it is served.
/v2/livescores?sport=A match that ended leaves at once; a match that just started joins within about a minute.
/v2/fixtures/{id} (other fields)About a minute while in play; final once finished. Before kick-off: a new start time or a postponement is picked up on the first request after the source announces it.
/v2/fixtures/{id}/lineups, statistics, events, play-by-play, best-players, momentum, shotmap, points, scorecard, average-positions, heatmap, form, streaksAbout 30 seconds while in play (at most 90); settled once finished. On a fixture:{id} WebSocket channel (Business) events, statistics and lineups are pushed when they change: events about 20–45 seconds after a goal, red card or period change (when the source’s REST lists it), otherwise within about 30 seconds; statistics and lineups within about 30–60 seconds.
fixture:{id} WebSocket play by play, momentum, shot map (Business)Play by play about 20 seconds after the source lists an entry (football, basketball); momentum and shot map about 30 seconds (football); a last push after full time.
/v2/fixtures/{id}/umpires, weather, gamesAbout 30 seconds (at most 90) while the match is in play; before it, up to 13 minutes; once finished, up to 30 hours.
/v2/fixtures/{id}/h2h, /h2h/fixturesRefreshed after the fixture ends; otherwise up to 30 hours. Status and score of the listed fixtures are brought up to the live feed when served.
/v2/fixtures/{id}/win-probabilityRecomputed at most every 15 seconds while in play, from the events, shot map and momentum above (about 30 seconds old); final and kept once finished. The pre-match estimate is fixed at kick-off.
/v2/fixtures/{id}/commentaryAn entry usually appears within a minute of the event (the events above are about 30 seconds old, then a few seconds to write it); written while someone follows the match — and always for the featured top-league matches shown on sportsapi.app/live — and never rewritten.
/v2/fixtures?date= (which fixtures a day holds)A fixture moved to another day, postponed or ended is refreshed on the next request, on both days. Otherwise a few minutes for today and ahead (at most 13); hours for past days, never once every fixture is finished.
/v2/teams/{id}/fixturesA match joins recent on the first request after kick-off; both lists refresh on the first request after one of the team’s matches ends, is moved or is postponed; otherwise up to 13 minutes (upcoming) or 2.5 hours (recent).
/v2/leagues/{id}/fixturesWhich fixtures a round lists: refreshed after one of them ends, is moved or is postponed; otherwise up to 13 minutes.
Start time and postponement of a fixture not yet started — wherever a Fixture appearsA new start time or a postponement we have seen (on the live feed or in any response from the source) is applied to every list holding the fixture when it is served.
/v2/players/{id}/fixtures, /seasons, /statisticsRefreshed after a match the player was in the lineup — or the squad — of ends (the request after the next one sees it; the source updates season statistics with a delay); the fixtures list also when such a match is moved or postponed. A new match in the fixtures list otherwise up to 13 minutes; seasons and statistics up to 6 hours.
/v2/referees/{id}, /v2/managers/{id}, /v2/teams/{id}/trophies, /v2/teams/{id}/career-statisticsUp to 6 hours, rarely up to 30.
/v2/referees/{id}/fixtures, /v2/managers/{id}/fixturesUp to 13 minutes; the status, score and clock of a match in play are current to the second.
/v2/teams/{id}/position-history, the form column of /v2/leagues/{id}/standingsRefreshed on the first request after a match of the season ends; otherwise up to 2.5 hours.
/v2/leagues/{id}/standingsRefreshed on the first request after a match of the season ends, and again 2 minutes later (the source can lag the final whistle); otherwise up to 13 minutes.
/v2/leagues/{id}/cup-treesRefreshed on the first request after a match of the season ends; otherwise up to 13 minutes.
/v2/leagues/{id}/top-players, top-teams, /v2/teams/{id}/statisticsRefreshed after a match of the season ends (the request after the next one sees it); the source itself updates these with a delay.
/v2/teams/{id}/squad, /v2/players/{id} (the current team)Refreshed on the next request once a move shows anywhere we look: a lineup naming a player the squad lacks, a squad or profile we refetch, or a transfers list. The transfers lists of teams read in the last 7 days are checked once a day, so their squads and profiles follow a move within about a day. Otherwise up to 6 hours, rarely up to 30 — the source does not announce transfers.
/v2/rankings/{type}, /v2/categories, /v2/leagues (directory), /v2/series (directory), /v2/teams/{id}/leagues, /v2/leagues/{id}/player-statisticsUp to 6 hours, rarely up to 30. The player-statistics explorer is not refreshed after a match — the source updates season statistics with a delay anyway.
/v2/races, /v2/races/{id}On a race:{id} WebSocket channel (Business, since 2026-10-24) changes are pushed: the race within about 60 seconds, a running session’s results within about 30. Over REST: while a session runs or starts within 15 minutes: about 30 seconds (at most 90); before: up to 13 minutes; once every session is over: up to 30 hours.
/v2/races/{id}/resultsFollows the session it classifies (without session=, the race): while it runs or starts within 15 minutes, about 30 seconds (at most 90); finished: up to 13 minutes while rows still change, up to 30 hours once nothing changed for 6 hours; not started yet: up to 13 minutes.
/v2/series/{id}/standings, /v2/series/{id}/racesUp to 13 minutes while rows still change; up to 30 hours once nothing changed for 6 hours (a season’s race list: once every race is over).
Transfers, seasons, rounds, searchUp to 6 hours, rarely up to 30 (a key nobody asked for in a day is served once more while it refreshes); search up to 13 minutes. The source’s transfer lists are current to the day.

Catalog

GET

/v2/sports

Every supported sport with its current in-progress match count (matches the source never closed — no change for 45 min and started longer ago than the sport can last — are not counted). kind says which endpoint family holds the sport’s data: fixtures (the Fixtures, Teams and Leagues endpoints) or races (motorsport and cycling — the Race sports endpoints; their fixture lists stay empty).

data
{ slug: string; name: string; kind: "fixtures" | "races"; live: number }[]
meta
count
cURLTry it →
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" \
    "https://api.sportsapi.app/v2/sports"
Example
{ "data": [ { "slug": "football", "name": "Football", "kind": "fixtures", "live": 42 }, { "slug": "ice-hockey", "name": "Ice hockey", "kind": "fixtures", "live": 9 }, …,
    { "slug": "motorsport", "name": "Motorsport", "kind": "races", "live": 0 } ],
  "meta": { "count": 20 } }

Live scores

In-progress fixtures. For a live layer, prefer the WebSocket — it pushes the same objects plus deltas.

GET

/v2/livescores

All in-progress fixtures across every sport, or one sport’s in-play board with ?sport= (each listed match as the live index holds it — the same state as the no-sport form and the WebSocket). Stale rows (no change for 45 min and started longer ago than the sport can last) are left out, here and on the WebSocket.

Parameters

sport
query
a sport slug from /v2/sports, e.g. football
data
Fixture[]
meta
count, plus sport when filtered
errors
400 bad_request — unknown sport
cURLTry it →
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" \
    "https://api.sportsapi.app/v2/livescores"

Fixtures

Fixtures by date, a single match, and its detail sub-resources.

GET

/v2/fixtures

Fixtures kicking off on one UTC calendar day — for one league, or for a whole sport ten leagues per page (in the order the leagues are ranked).

Parameters

date
queryrequired
a UTC day, YYYY-MM-DD (1990-01-01 up to a year ahead)
sport
query
a sport slug — required unless league is given
league
query
a league id: that league’s fixtures that day (one page; page must be 0)
page
query
with sport only: page index 0–99 (default 0), 10 leagues per page
data
Fixture[]
meta
date, page, count, hasNextPage; with league: league (+ sport if given), page always 0 and hasNextPage false; with sport: sport, leagueCount (leagues on this page), complete (false when some league lists could not be fetched right now — retry shortly)
errors
400 bad_request — missing/invalid date, unknown sport, neither sport nor league, page not 0–99, page other than 0 with league503 upstream_unavailable — none of the page’s league lists could be fetched
Walk pages until hasNextPage is false. Every page but the last holds 10 leagues, so a page with no league means the day is over; a page can still hold fewer fixtures than leagues (a league whose matches fall just outside the UTC day contributes none). Which fixtures a day holds is cached for minutes (today and ahead) or hours (past days; for good once every fixture is finished); the status, score and clock of a fixture in play are current to the second (see Data freshness). For a live feed use /v2/livescores or the WebSocket.
ExampleTry it →
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" "https://api.sportsapi.app/v2/fixtures?date=2026-10-18&sport=football"

{ "data": [ { "id": 201324, "sport": "football", "status": { "type": "finished", … },
    "startTime": "2026-10-18T15:30:00.000Z", "league": { "id": 195828, "name": "Premier League", … }, … }, … ],
  "meta": { "date": "2026-10-18", "sport": "football", "page": 0, "count": 38, "leagueCount": 10,
            "hasNextPage": true, "complete": true } }
GET

/v2/fixtures/{id}

Full fixture: teams, score, status, match clock, league, season, round, venue, winner, the referee (with career cards per game), both managers (homeManager / awayManager), previousLegFixtureId (our id of the first leg or previous series game) and aggregateWinner (on a finished second leg, the side that went through) — plus sport extras: seeds (homeSeed / awaySeed), tennis serving (the side serving now) and surface (hard / clay / grass / carpet, indoor), cricket note, battingSide, toss (winner, bat / bowl), umpires and tvUmpire, MMA / boxing fightResult (method, round, and the time of a stoppage), fightDiscipline (boxing, kickboxing, muayThai, … when the source tags it) and fightCard (main card / prelims, order, weight class), attendance (spectators, when reported), matchFormat (darts best of sets / legs, esports best of games), baseball inningState (inning, top / bottom, count, outs, runners) and basketball timeouts (left per side).

Parameters

id
pathrequired
our numeric id (positive integer)
data
Fixture
Every part of a score is in periods: football and futsal extra time as periods.extra1 / extra2, every other sport’s overtime as periods.overtime, baseball extra innings as period10, period11, …; current never counts a shoot-out (penalties does — in ice hockey current includes the one goal credited for a shoot-out win). status.description is our own label (“After penalties”, “After extra time”, “After overtime”, “Game 1”, …). A fixture whose coverage the source cancelled is status canceled with empty score sides. A match finished on penalties has the shoot-out winner as winner — on a second leg too, where the night’s result stays in normalTime; aggregateWinner says who went through on aggregate (null when the source does not settle a level aggregate; lists and WebSocket snapshots may carry null — read it here). referee, homeManager / awayManager, toss, umpires, tvUmpire, previousLegFixtureId, fightCard and attendance are filled here only: fixture lists, the live board and WebSocket snapshots carry them as null (surface also on the live tennis board). inningState and timeouts are set only while the match is in play (null otherwise) and arrive in WebSocket deltas (inningState whole, timeouts partial; null when play stops) — the source re-sends the baseball state about once a minute, so the count can lag. fightResult arrives in a WebSocket delta of its own, usually after the finishing one (the source publishes it ~20–60 s after the winner). Rugby periods fill while live: period1 at half-time, period2 = current − period1 during the second half. Esports periods: CS = 1 for each map won (0 otherwise), LoL = the side’s kills in game N. serving replaces firstToServe (same value, kept for now, deprecated).
cURLTry it →
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" \
    "https://api.sportsapi.app/v2/fixtures/{id}"
Example

GET

/v2/fixtures/{id}/lineups

Lineups, formations and missing players, with each player’s match rating and statistics.

Parameters

id
pathrequired
our numeric id (positive integer)
data
Lineups
Coverage is graded per fixture: top leagues have lineups (and per-player ratings and statistics), many youth, amateur and friendly matches never get them. A player’s statistics use the same keys as the team statistics where they mean the same thing (passes, accuratePasses, shotsOnGoal, tackles, …; bigChancesCreated = big chances he made for a teammate); every …Percentage is a 0–100 share, except basketball’s trueShootingPercentage, which can pass 100 (a few free throws and a three). rating and statistics are null for a player who did not play; avgRating (football) is the player’s season average, listed mostly before and around kick-off. position is a word per sport (G is a goalkeeper in football, a goalie in ice hockey, a guard in basketball); positionCode keeps the source letter. A fixture without lineups (yet) returns 200 with confirmed: false and empty sides — 404 only for an id that does not exist. During a live match this is refreshed about every 30 seconds.
cURLTry it →
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" \
    "https://api.sportsapi.app/v2/fixtures/{id}/lineups"
Example
{ "data": { "confirmed": true,
    "home": { "formation": "4-2-3-1", "players": [
      { "player": { "id": 3772, "name": "David Raya", "slug": "david-raya", "shortName": "D. Raya", "image": "…" },
        "position": "goalkeeper", "positionCode": "G", "jerseyNumber": "1", "substitute": false, "captain": false,
        "rating": 7.1, "avgRating": 6.94, "ratingVersions": { "original": 7.1, "alternative": 7.3 }, "star": null, "battingOrder": null,
        "statistics": { "minutesPlayed": 90, "passes": 34, "accuratePasses": 29, "saves": 2, "touches": 41, … } }, … ],
      "missing": [ { "player": { … }, "availability": "out", "reason": "injury", "description": "Knee Injury",
                     "expectedReturnAt": "2026-11-02T00:00:00.000Z" } ] },
    "away": { … } } }
GET

/v2/fixtures/{id}/statistics

Match statistics grouped by period and category.

Parameters

id
pathrequired
our numeric id (positive integer)
data
Statistics
Same graded coverage as lineups, and it deepens as a match progresses: a lower-tier fixture may carry only cards, a top league the full set of groups. Keys are one vocabulary across sports (totalShots, shotsOnGoal, passes, fouls, …; every key per sport is in the reference’s Statistic keys), group keys a fixed table per sport. American football: the team’s passingNetYards and passingYardsPerAttempt are the source’s gross figures (sacks not taken off) — the players’ own passingNetYards in the lineups are net. A fixture with no statistics (yet — e.g. not started) returns 200 with { "periods": [] }; 404 only for an id that does not exist. Refreshed about every 30 seconds while the match is live.

/v2/fixtures/{id}/events

Incidents — goals, cards, substitutions, period markers, added-time boards — oldest first (chronological).

Parameters

id
pathrequired
our numeric id (positive integer)
data
Incident[]
meta
count
An empty array when the fixture has no events (yet). An injuryTime incident carries the announced added minutes in addedMinute. minute is null off the clock (before kick-off, at half-time, on the bench, in a shoot-out — shoot-out kicks come last, in kick order: shootoutSequence 1…N across both sides, shootoutRound = the taker’s side’s 1st, 2nd, … kick). A period row means that period ended (its period is the one that ended; the period still being played has none), and on set sports its homeScore / awayScore are sets won so far. Every incident’s period is set. Every field is present on every incident (null when it does not apply to the type); type and detail are closed enums. A football goal carries buildUp: the passes, crosses and shots that led to it (side, player, minute, pitch position and end position, assist, body part, expected goals), the goal last; [] on every other incident and where the source has none. Cricket ball-by-ball and the per-point rows of set sports are not listed. Refreshed about every 30 seconds while the match is live.

/v2/fixtures/{id}/win-probability

Our own win-probability model for a football fixture: the pre-match estimate, the current home / draw / away probabilities and the curve — a point at kick-off, every minute, and right after each goal, red card, period start / end and big missed chance (reason bigChance), each with the UTC instant it describes (at). Pro and Business plans.

Parameters

id
pathrequired
our numeric id (positive integer)
since
query
an ISO-8601 instant (any offset): only the curve points whose at is after it — for clients that poll; current is always returned
data
WinProbability
meta
count (points in series), since (when given)
errors
403 endpoint_not_in_plan — Free and Starter keys404 not_supported — not a football fixture
An analysis indicator, not betting advice: no bookmaker odds go into it. Model v3 (since 2026-10-25; v2 since 2026-10-22), transparent: pre-match expected goals per side from both teams’ last 30 results in all competitions (domestic league and European cups, each against the opponent’s strength), their domestic league tables (goals for / against per game, shrunk towards the league average) and our league-strength coefficients, which put teams of different leagues on one scale — fitted on three seasons of European cup matches — then blended with the current competition’s own table as it fills up (a European campaign two games old leans on the teams’ overall strength, a league 30 games in on its table), the last five results and home advantage (none in a final). On our backtest (over 8,000 league and 1,500 European matches, held out by season) this beat v1 in both: most in European ties and early in a season. One exception, since v3: a league match with a newcomer (a side promoted or relegated into the competition, early in a season) uses the current table and form only — the newcomer’s strength on its old league’s scale misled the estimate. Fixtures whose pre-match estimate was fixed under an older model keep that model (v1 and v2 share the in-play part). In play, the goals still to come are Poisson for each side over the time left (added time included; goals get likelier as a match goes on), cut for a side down to ten men (and raised for its opponent), and tilted for the next half hour by the last ten minutes of attack momentum — constants fitted on 1,080 finished matches of 12 competitions and checked on the following season. Since v3 the in-play outcome is calibrated (made slightly less certain — the curve was a little over-confident on that backtest), phased in over the first 15 minutes so the kick-off point equals the pre-match estimate. The shot map’s live expected goals are not blended into the scoring rate — on that backtest they added nothing measurable — but a big missed chance still marks a point on the curve. home + draw + away = 1; draw means level on the scoreboard at the end (extra time counted, a shoot-out not). Not started: the pre-match estimate and an empty series; finished: 1 / 0 / 0 and the full curve, kept for good. The pre-match estimate is fixed once the match starts. History with time: every point carries at — the moment of the match it describes (the end of that minute, the goal, the whistle), measured from the running match clock, else estimated from the kick-off with a 15-minute half-time; non-decreasing along the curve; current.at is when the estimate was computed (the end of the match once finished). A point is stored once it is two minutes old and never changed after, so the curve shows what the model said at the time. Polling: pass since = your newest at minus two minutes (the newest two minutes can still gain a point the source lists late) and replace your points after since with the answer. Live updates: fixture:{id} WebSocket channels (Business) get a winProbability frame when an outcome moves at least one percentage point.
cURLTry it →
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" \
    "https://api.sportsapi.app/v2/fixtures/{id}/win-probability"
Example
{ "data": { "fixtureId": 211521, "model": "v3", "updatedAt": "2026-10-18T16:02:11.000Z",
    "prematch": { "home": 0.4521, "draw": 0.2655, "away": 0.2824, "homeExpectedGoals": 1.52, "awayExpectedGoals": 1.13, "standings": true, "form": true, "allCompetitions": true, "domesticTables": true },
    "current": { "home": 1, "draw": 0, "away": 0, "minute": 90, "addedMinute": 4, "homeScore": 5, "awayScore": 0, "at": "2026-10-18T15:54:00.000Z" },
    "series": [ { "home": 0.4521, "draw": 0.2655, "away": 0.2824, "minute": 0, "addedMinute": null, "homeScore": 0, "awayScore": 0, "at": "2026-10-18T14:00:00.000Z", "reason": "kickoff" },
      { "home": 0.5983, "draw": 0.2388, "away": 0.1629, "minute": 4, "addedMinute": null, "homeScore": 1, "awayScore": 0, "at": "2026-10-18T14:03:30.000Z", "reason": "goal" }, …,
      { "home": 1, "draw": 0, "away": 0, "minute": 90, "addedMinute": 4, "homeScore": 5, "awayScore": 0, "at": "2026-10-18T15:54:00.000Z", "reason": "final" } ],
    "inputs": { "shotmap": true, "momentum": true, "events": true } },
  "meta": { "count": 104 } }

/v2/fixtures/{id}/commentary

AI match commentary for a football fixture, oldest first (by seq; the newest 100): one short entry per goal, red card, missed penalty, VAR decision, period start / end, big chance and sustained momentum swing (events of the same few seconds share one entry), plus half-time and full-time summaries. Pro and Business plans.

Parameters

id
pathrequired
our numeric id (positive integer)
data
Commentary
meta
count, generatedBy
errors
403 endpoint_not_in_plan — Free and Starter keys404 not_supported — not a football fixture
Written by Claude (Anthropic) from our own data of the match only — events, score, clock, shot map, statistics and our win-probability model; no betting language. Generated while someone follows the match: this endpoint, a fixture:{id} WebSocket channel or the public showcase keep it going, so call it during the match (a match nobody followed has no entries); the featured top-league matches of sportsapi.app/live are always written. Each entry is written once and is the same for every client; seq never changes. kind is one of kickoff, goal, redCard, missedPenalty, varDecision, bigChance, momentum, periodStart, periodEnd, halfTime, fullTime, update; a fullTime summary carries minute 90 (120 after extra time). Live updates: fixture:{id} channels (Business) get a commentary frame per new entry.

      { "seq": 2, "kind": "goal", "minute": 36, "addedMinute": null, "model": "claude-sonnet-5-5", "createdAt": "2026-10-18T13:37:41.000Z",
        "text": "Nico Paz doubles Como's lead, finishing after a pass from Álex Valle, four minutes after Mattia Liberali's opener. Our model now gives Como an 85% win probability, up from 65%." },
      { "seq": 3, "kind": "halfTime", "minute": 45, "addedMinute": null, "model": "claude-sonnet-5-5", "createdAt": "2026-10-18T13:52:04.000Z",
        "text": "Como lead Fiorentina 2-1 at the break. Mattia Liberali and Nico Paz struck in the 32nd and 36th minutes before Marin Pongračić pulled one back, a goal confirmed by VAR in first-half stoppage time." } ] },
  "meta": { "count": 3, "generatedBy": "claude" } }

Every shot with its outcome and expected goals, oldest first: football (expectedGoals / expectedGoalsOnTarget, situation, body part, pitch and goal-mouth coordinates), ice hockey (technique, strength, rink coordinates) and basketball (every field-goal attempt: made / missed / blocked and where on the court).

pathrequired

data
Shot[]
meta
count
Football, ice hockey and basketball, covered leagues; an empty array otherwise. outcome is goal | save | miss | block | post in football and ice hockey; basketball uses goal (made), miss and block, its position is in tenths of a foot from the basket, player and time are null, and home shots come before away shots; goalType is regular | ownGoal | penalty; technique (wrist, snap, slap, …) and strength are ice hockey only. Shoot-out kicks come last: shootoutSequence is the kick order across both sides (as on the events), shootoutRound the taker’s side’s 1st, 2nd, … kick. Football period (since 2026-10-24; null before) follows the minute: period1, period2, extra1, extra2, penalties for shoot-out kicks. Refreshed about every 30 seconds while the match is live; on a fixture:{id} WebSocket channel (Business) the whole list is pushed as a shotmap frame when it changes.

/v2/fixtures/{id}/points

The match point by point. Tennis: sets → games (server, winner, set score) → points. Volleyball, table tennis, badminton: sets → rallies with the running score. Cricket: innings → overs → balls (outcome, runs, extras, wicket and dismissal, batter, bowler, score after the ball). Baseball: at-bats (inning, top / bottom, batting side, batter, pitcher, the home win probability before and after). Darts: sets → legs (start score, who threw first, winner, checkout) → visits (score of the visit, both sides’ remaining, checkout).

Parameters

id
pathrequired
our numeric id (positive integer)
data
Points
format says which list is filled (sets for tennis and rally sports, innings for cricket, atBats for baseball, darts for darts — the others are empty). Darts visits carry no individual darts (the source has none); a legs match is one set. Baseball at-bats come with the source’s own home win probability (0–100, not our model) and no outcome (the source gives none). Other sports, and a match without point-by-point yet: 200 with format null and empty lists. Rally sports list the rallies the source recorded — lower tiers can miss some (the running score shows the gap). Tennis points carry the score after the point (homeScore / awayScore: "15", "A"; null on the appended game-winning point), description (ace, doubleFault) and homeType / awayType (won, breakPoint, setPoint, miniBreak, none); a match tie-break is the deciding set’s only game, counted to 10. Refreshed about every 30 seconds while the match is live.
cURLTry it →
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" \
    "https://api.sportsapi.app/v2/fixtures/{id}/points"
Example

          "wicket": true, "dismissal": "bowled", "batter": { "id": 886956, "name": "Asitha Fernando", … },
          "bowler": { "id": 975942, "name": "Haris Rauf", … }, "fielder": null,
          "dismissedBatter": { "id": 886956, … }, "scoreRuns": 268, "scoreWickets": 10 } ] } ] } ] } }

GET

/v2/fixtures/{id}/scorecard

Cricket: the full scorecard, innings by innings — totals, extras, the batting card (state, dismissal, bowler, fielder, runs, balls, fours, sixes, strike rate), the bowling card (overs, maidens, runs, wickets, wides, no-balls, economy), falls of wicket and partnerships.

Parameters

id
pathrequired
our numeric id (positive integer)
data
Scorecard
Cricket only: other sports, and a match before its first ball, return 200 with an empty innings list. Overs use cricket notation (19.3 = 19 overs and 3 balls; a completed over is 5, never the source’s 4.6 — falls of wicket included). Multi-day matches often list no partnerships. Refreshed about every 30 seconds while the match is live. current (CricketState) is the crease of the innings in play — striker, non-striker, bowler, over and ball — derived by us from the ball-by-ball, not taken from the source’s own current-batsman field (which is unreliable); null when no innings is in play or the match has no ball-by-ball coverage, and its batters are briefly null right after a delivery while the ball-by-ball and the scorecard disagree. A run out is the one ambiguous case (which end the batter was out at).
cURLTry it →
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" \
    "https://api.sportsapi.app/v2/fixtures/{id}/scorecard"
Example
{ "data": { "innings": [ { "inning": "inning1", "battingSide": "away",
      "battingTeam": { "id": 207233, "name": "West Indies", … }, "bowlingTeam": { "id": 207238, "name": "India", … },
      "runs": 247, "wickets": 3, "overs": 20,
      "extras": { "total": 18, "wides": 13, "noBalls": 1, "byes": 0, "legByes": 4, "penalties": 0 },
      "batting": [ { "batter": { "id": 880113, "name": "Shai Hope", … }, "state": "notOut", "dismissal": null,
                     "description": "Not out", "bowler": null, "fielder": null,
                     "runs": 102, "balls": 50, "fours": 4, "sixes": 9, "strikeRate": 204 },
                   { "batter": { "name": "Shimron Hetmyer", … }, "state": "out", "dismissal": "caughtAndBowled",
                     "description": "Caught & Bowled", "bowler": { "name": "Prince Yadav", … },
                     "fielder": { "name": "Prince Yadav", … }, "runs": 33, "balls": 12, … }, … ],
      "bowling": [ { "bowler": { "name": "Arshdeep Singh", … }, "overs": 4, "maidens": 0, "runs": 52,
                     "wickets": 1, "wides": 6, "noBalls": 0, "economy": 13 }, … ],
      "fallOfWickets": [ { "wicket": 1, "runs": 52, "overs": 4.2, "batter": { "name": "Jewel Andrew", … } }, … ],
      "partnerships": [ { "batter1": { "name": "Shai Hope", … }, "batter2": { "name": "Jewel Andrew", … },
                          "runs": 52, "balls": 27 }, … ] }, … ],
    "current": null } }

// In play — the crease, derived from the ball-by-ball:
    "current": { "inning": "inning1", "battingSide": "home", "striker": { "name": "Emma de Broughe", … },
                 "nonStriker": { "name": "Ellie Johnston", … }, "bowler": null, "over": 3, "ball": 0 }

/v2/fixtures/{id}/games

Esports: the series game by game — status, map, start and duration, winner, and per side the score, players (role, champion / hero, kills, deaths, assists, then the title’s own figures — League of Legends gold, creep score, level; Dota 2 last hits, denies, net worth, gold and experience per minute; Counter-Strike ADR, headshot kills, KAST, K − D, first-kill difference, flash assists), bans and objectives (towers, dragons, barons, barracks, …).

Parameters

id
pathrequired
our numeric id (positive integer)
data
EsportsGame[]
meta
count
errors
403 history_not_in_plan — the fixture is older than your plan’s history
Esports only: other sports return 200 with an empty array. map is null for titles with one map (League of Legends). Which player and objective fields are filled depends on the title (gold, dragons and barons are League of Legends; denies, netWorth, goldPerMinute, experiencePerMinute, barracks and firstBlood Dota 2; averageDamagePerRound, headshotKills, kastPercentage, killDeathDifference, firstKillDifference and flashAssists Counter-Strike); a field the source does not keep for that title is null. Counter-Strike has no bans or objectives, and a map in play has no lineup yet — the figures appear some minutes after the map ends.

GET

/v2/teams/{id}/fixtures

A page of the team’s recent or upcoming fixtures.

Parameters

id
pathrequired
our numeric id (positive integer)
type
query
recent | upcoming (default upcoming)
page
query
page index, an integer 0–50 (default 0)
data
Fixture[]
meta
type, page, count, hasNextPage
errors
400 bad_request — type not recent|upcoming, or page not an integer 0–50
A known team with nothing in the list answers 200 with an empty array. One rule for every competitor list (since 2026-10-24): upcoming = not started (or postponed to a date ahead), soonest first — page 0 also picks up a next match the source files under recent (tennis players, fighters); recent = in play, finished or called off, newest first on every page. The status, score and clock of a match in play (or just finished) are current to the second; a match that kicks off appears in recent on the next request, and both lists are refreshed on the first request after one of the team’s matches ends, is moved or is postponed (see Data freshness).
cURLTry it →
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" \
    "https://api.sportsapi.app/v2/teams/{id}/fixtures"
Example
{ "data": [ { "id": 202006, "status": { "type": "finished", … }, … } ],
  "meta": { "type": "recent", "page": 0, "count": 30, "hasNextPage": true } }
GET

/v2/teams/{id}/transfers

The team’s moves in (arrivals) and out (departures), about the last year, newest first: transfers with their fee, loans and loan ends, and the US leagues’ roster moves — signings, trades, the draft, waivers, 10-day contracts.

Parameters

id
pathrequired
our numeric id (positive integer)
data
TeamTransfers
meta
arrivalCount, departureCount
A move names both teams when the source lists them; a free agent’s signing has no from, a waiver no to (fromName / toName still carry the source’s name of a side it does not list). fee is set only when the source states one; freeTransfer marks a free move. Empty lists where the source has none.
cURLTry it →
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" \
    "https://api.sportsapi.app/v2/teams/{id}/transfers"
Example
{ "data": { "arrivals": [ { "player": { "id": 4120, "name": "Iliman Ndiaye", "slug": "iliman-ndiaye", "shortName": "I. Ndiaye", "image": "…" },
      "type": "transfer", "date": "2026-09-01",
      "from": { "id": 3901, "name": "Everton", … }, "fromName": "Everton",
      "to": { "id": 3802, "name": "Manchester City", … }, "toName": "Manchester City",
      "fee": { "amount": 70000000, "currency": "EUR" }, "freeTransfer": false, "draft": null }, … ],
    "departures": [ { "player": { … }, "type": "loan", "date": "2026-09-02", "to": { "name": "Benfica", … }, "fee": null, … }, … ] },
  "meta": { "arrivalCount": 22, "departureCount": 23 } }

/v2/teams/{id}/statistics

The team’s season statistics in one league: totals and averages (goals scored and conceded, shots, possession, rating, clean sheets, …).

Parameters

id
pathrequired
our numeric id (positive integer)
league
queryrequired
a league id (e.g. the team’s fixtures’ league)
season
queryrequired
a season id from /v2/leagues/{id}/seasons
type
query
overall | home | away | regularSeason | playoffs. Default: the season’s own — overall where it has one (football), else regularSeason (NBA, NHL, …); meta.type says which was used
data
TeamSeasonStatistics
meta
league, season, type (the one used)
errors
400 bad_request — missing league or season, type not one of overall, home, away, regularSeason, playoffs404 no_data — the source has no statistics for that team, league, season and type (404 not_found: an id we never issued)404 not_found — season is not one of this league’s seasons (the message names the parameter; list them with /v2/leagues/{id}/seasons)
Keys follow the match statistics’ vocabulary (totalShots, shotsOnGoal, cornerKicks, passes, averageRating, …) with an Against twin for the opponents’ figures; a 0 matches beside non-zero counts is left out.
cURLTry it →
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" \
    "https://api.sportsapi.app/v2/teams/{id}/statistics?league=…&season=…"
Example
{ "data": { "statistics": { "matches": 7, "goalsScored": 19, "goalsConceded": 7, "totalShots": 112,
                            "averageBallPossession": 61.3, "averageRating": 7.02, "cleanSheets": 3, … } },
  "meta": { "league": 195828, "season": 200386, "type": "overall" } }

A page of the player’s most recent fixtures (the teams he played for), newest first on every page (since 2026-10-24). /v2/leagues/{id}/standings

Standings for one season. By default the season’s primary table (the league table, or the first group of a group stage — meta.overall says whether it holds every team); with group=all every table (conferences, divisions, groups); with type=home or away the table of home games or away games only.

Parameters

id
pathrequired
our numeric id (positive integer)
season
queryrequired
a season id from /v2/leagues/{id}/seasons
group
query
all → every table of the season as StandingsGroup[]
type
query
overall (every game, default), home (home games only) or away (away games only); total is still accepted for one release and answered as overall
data
StandingsRow[] (default) | StandingsGroup[] (group=all)
meta
season, type, source (upstream = the source’s table, computed = built by us from the fixtures), count (rows; tables with group=all); by default also group (the table’s name), groupCount (tables in the season), overall (whether this table holds every team), tieBreakRule, scoreUnit
errors
400 bad_request — missing or invalid season, group other than all, type other than overall|home|away404 no_data — the source has no such table for that season (e.g. a home / away table it does not publish, outside basketball, ice hockey and American football); 404 not_found — an id we never issued404 not_found — season is not one of this league’s seasons (the message names the parameter; list them with /v2/leagues/{id}/seasons)
Some seasons have several tables, in the source’s order — the NHL has two conferences, four divisions and the league; MLS two conferences and the overall table; a World Cup one per group. Exactly one table is primary (the default: the league table where there is one, otherwise the one with the most teams; the first group when all are equal); overall is true only on a table that holds every team of the season. position is always 1..n (re-ranked by us when the source’s is not). Columns that do not apply to the sport are null: points is null in the NBA (it ranks by winPercentage); draws is null wherever a table cannot draw (basketball, ice hockey, baseball, volleyball, …); overtimeLosses is set in ice hockey; scoresFor / scoresAgainst count scoreUnit (goals, points, runs, sets, …); streak (+3 = three wins in a row, −2 = two losses) is set where the source has it (NBA, EuroLeague, Liga ACB, …). form (since 2026-10-24) is the team’s last results in this competition season, up to five, oldest first (home / away tables: home / away results only); null where the source has none. Home / away tables exist for football and for basketball, handball, volleyball and ice-hockey leagues such as the EuroLeague, Liga ACB, the Handball-Bundesliga, the SuperLega and the KHL. The NBA and the NHL publish none, and the NFL’s stop updating: for basketball, ice hockey and American football we compute them (meta.source computed) from the season’s finished regular-season fixtures — home rows from home games, away rows from away games — with the columns of the total table that the same computation over every game reproduces exactly (NBA: wins, losses, winPercentage, gamesBehind per table, scores; NHL: wins, losses, overtimeLosses = overtime + shoot-out, points = 2 per win + 1 per overtime loss, scores; NFL: wins, losses, draws, winPercentage, scores). A published home / away table in those sports that is missing games is replaced by the computed one. winPercentage counts a tie as half a win. Ties are ranked by points or win share, then wins and score difference, not by head-to-head. Refreshed daily.
cURLTry it →
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" \
    "https://api.sportsapi.app/v2/leagues/{id}/standings?season=…"
Example
{ "data": [ { "position": 1, "team": { "id": 4438, "name": "Manchester City", … },
    "played": 7, "wins": 7, "draws": 0, "losses": 0, "overtimeWins": null, "overtimeLosses": null,
    "scoresFor": 19, "scoresAgainst": 7, "scoreDifference": 12, "points": 21,
    "winPercentage": null, "gamesBehind": null, "zone": "Champions League", "form": ["win", "win", "win", "win", "win"] }, … ],
  "meta": { "season": 200386, "type": "overall", "source": "upstream", "group": "Premier League 26/27", "groupCount": 1,
            "count": 20, "overall": true, "tieBreakRule": null, "scoreUnit": "goals" } }

/v2/leagues/{id}/top-players

Season leaderboards: the top players per statistic (rating, goals, xG, assists, tackles, saves, … — up to 50 each at the source), paged: limit players per leaderboard (default 10), or one leaderboard with category.

Parameters

id
pathrequired
our numeric id (positive integer)
season
queryrequired
a season id from /v2/leagues/{id}/seasons
type
query
overall | home | away | regularSeason | playoffs. Default: the season’s own — overall where it has one (football), else regularSeason (NBA, NHL, …); meta.type says which was used
category
query
one leaderboard only (a category of this season, e.g. goals); unknown → 400 listing the season’s categories
limit
query
entries per leaderboard, 1–50 (default 10)
page
query
page of limit entries, 0–49 (default 0 = the leaders)
data
TopPlayersCategory[]
meta
season, type (the one used), category (null = all), limit, page, count (categories), hasNextPage (some leaderboard has more after this page)
errors
400 bad_request — missing or invalid season, type not one of overall, home, away, regularSeason, playoffs, limit outside 1–50, page outside 0–49, or an unknown category (the message lists the season’s categories)404 not_found — season is not one of this league’s seasons (the message names the parameter; list them with /v2/leagues/{id}/seasons)
Every leaderboard is cut to the same places: page 1 with limit 10 is places 11–20 in each. For the full top 50 of one statistic ask category=goals&limit=50 (one leaderboard, ~20 KB) instead of every leaderboard at once (football: 32 leaderboards, ~550 KB at 50 each). Categories vary by sport (football ~30; basketball points, rebounds, assists, …) and are named with the statistic keys (averageRating, goals, cleanSheets, goalInvolvements, …); statistic is the key in each entry’s statistics the board ranks (football mostConceded / leastConceded rank goalsConceded). Without type the season’s default is used (regularSeason in the NBA, NHL, …). A league, season or type without leaderboards returns an empty array.
cURLTry it →
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" \
    "https://api.sportsapi.app/v2/leagues/{id}/top-players?season=…"

  "meta": { "season": 200386, "type": "overall", "category": null, "limit": 10, "page": 0, "count": 32, "hasNextPage": true } }

The season’s player-statistics explorer (football): every player of the league, 20 a page, sorted by any statistic, with a group of columns — summary, attack, defense, passing, goalkeeping or other — and filters by position and team. Football leagues only: the source has no such explorer for other sports (checked 2026-10-28 on the NBA, NHL and EuroLeague), so their leagues answer 404 not_supported — use /v2/leagues/{id}/top-players for their season leaders.

Parameters

pathrequired

query
desc (default) | asc
page
query

position
query

team

data
PlayerStatisticsRow[]
meta

errors

Keys are the season-statistic vocabulary (as in /v2/players/{id}/statistics); every row also carries appearances and minutesPlayed, and the order key when its group lacks it. Walk pages until hasNextPage is false (at most 50 pages = 1,000 players). For the top N of one statistic, /top-players is cheaper.

/v2/leagues/{id}/cup-trees

The season’s knockout brackets — a cup’s knockout stage, playoffs, a tennis draw: rounds → ties → the two participants (team, seed, winner, score) → our fixture ids.

Parameters

id
pathrequired

season

data
CupTree[]
meta

errors

score is the source’s figure for the tie: aggregate goals over two legs (football), games won in a series (basketball, ice hockey), sets (tennis); penalties = shoot-out goals. fromBlock is the order of the previous round’s tie the participant came from; team null = a placeholder slot (“winner of QF 1”); matchCount 0 = a bye. Discovery

Find the ids to start from: world rankings, and every league of a sport by country or category.

GET

/v2/rankings

The rankings we serve: FIFA (men), UEFA country and club coefficients, World Rugby (men), ATP and WTA singles (official and live) and the UFC divisions.

Parameters

sport
query
a sport slug: only that sport’s rankings
data
RankingTypeInfo[]
meta
count, plus sport when filtered
errors
400 bad_request — unknown sport
entry says what a row ranks: team (a national team or club), competitor (a player or fighter — a TeamRef, kind individual) or country. Our own catalogue: answered without a fetch.
cURLTry it →
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" \
    "https://api.sportsapi.app/v2/rankings"
Example
{ "data": [ { "type": "fifa-men", "name": "FIFA World Ranking (men)", "sport": "football", "gender": "male", "entry": "team" },
    { "type": "uefa-countries", "name": "UEFA country coefficients", "sport": "football", "gender": null, "entry": "country" }, …,
    { "type": "atp", "name": "ATP singles ranking", "sport": "tennis", "gender": "male", "entry": "competitor" }, … ],
  "meta": { "count": 19 } }

type
pathrequired
a type from /v2/rankings, e.g. atp, fifa-men, uefa-clubs, ufc-lightweight

RankingRow[]
meta
type, updatedAt (when the source last updated the table, or null), count
errors
404 not_found — unknown ranking type
team is the ranked team or competitor (null on UEFA country rows, whose league is the country’s top league and country the country). UFC divisions list the champion at position 0. Columns the source does not keep for a ranking are null.

Race sports

Motorsport and cycling (kind races in /v2/sports). A series is the league of race sports (Formula 1, MotoGP; in cycling the whole men’s or women’s calendar), a race is a Grand Prix weekend or a cycling race, a session one timed part of it (practice, qualifying, sprint, the race; a cycling stage). Drivers, riders and their teams are TeamRefs, so /v2/teams/{id} serves them. Times are milliseconds, distances metres. Not on the WebSocket yet — poll /v2/races/{id} and /results while a session runs.

GET

/v2/races

Races with a session starting on one UTC day, each with all its sessions.

Parameters

sport
queryrequired
motorsport | cycling
date
queryrequired
a UTC day, YYYY-MM-DD
data
Race[]
meta
date, sport, count, complete (false when some races could not be fetched right now — retry shortly)
errors
400 bad_request — missing or invalid date, sport not a race sport403 history_not_in_plan — a day before your plan’s history503 upstream_unavailable — none of the day’s races could be fetched
At most 40 races a day. A race weekend appears on every day one of its sessions starts. The source files some weekends twice under two series of one name (NASCAR Cup Series); the copy whose series has no seasons is left out of the day (its id still answers on /v2/races/{id}).
ExampleTry it →
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" "https://api.sportsapi.app/v2/races?sport=motorsport&date=2026-10-11"

{ "data": [ { "id": 812345, "name": "Singapore GP", "sport": "motorsport", "series": { "id": 812300, "name": "Formula 1", … },
    "status": "finished", "startDate": "2026-10-09", "endDate": "2026-10-11", "sessions": [ … ], … }, … ],
  "meta": { "date": "2026-10-11", "sport": "motorsport", "count": 3, "complete": true } }
GET

/v2/races/{id}

One race: series, season, round, status, days, host country, circuit (motorsport), laps and distance, category (cycling), winner — and its sessions in start order, each with type, status, start time, laps, distance, stage towns and profile (cycling), weather, track condition, temperatures, safety car and winner.

Parameters

id
pathrequired
our numeric id (positive integer)
data
Race
errors
403 history_not_in_plan — the race started before your plan’s history404 not_found — not a race id (a season or session id included)404 no_data — a duplicate copy the source files under a second series and never runs (NASCAR Cup); error.series and, when it can be matched, error.race name the real ones
startDate / endDate are UTC days; sessions carry exact times. winner is the winner of the main race (a cycling stage race: of the general classification), set once finished. circuit.lengthMeters and distanceMeters: Formula 1 and NASCAR (converted from miles); MotoGP has laps only — the source keeps neither its circuit length nor its race distance. A race without laps / distance of its own takes the main race session’s.
cURLTry it →
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" \
    "https://api.sportsapi.app/v2/races/{id}"
Example
{ "data": {
    "id": 812345, "name": "Singapore GP", "slug": "singapore-gp", "sport": "motorsport",
    "series": { "id": 812300, "name": "Formula 1", "slug": "formula-1", "sport": "motorsport" },
    "season": { "id": 812301, "name": "Formula 1 2026", "year": "2026", "startYear": 2026, "endYear": 2026 },
    "round": 17, "status": "finished", "startDate": "2026-10-09", "endDate": "2026-10-11",
    "country": { "code": "SG", "name": "Singapore" },
    "circuit": { "name": "Marina Bay", "city": "Singapore", "country": { "code": "SG", "name": "Singapore" }, "lengthMeters": 4927 },
    "laps": 62, "distanceMeters": 305337, "category": null,
    "winner": { "id": 700001, "name": "Max Verstappen", "slug": "verstappen-max", "shortName": "M. Verstappen", "code": "VER", "image": "https://cdn.sportsapi.app/v2/teams/700001/logo" },
    "sessions": [ …,
      { "id": 812350, "name": "Grand Prix", "type": "race", "status": "finished", "startTime": "2026-10-11T12:00:00.000Z",
        "laps": 62, "lapsCompleted": 62, "distanceMeters": 305337, "departureCity": null, "arrivalCity": null, "profile": null,
        "weather": "night", "trackCondition": "dry", "airTemperatureC": 30.2, "trackTemperatureC": 41.5, "humidityPercent": 77.4,
        "safetyCar": null, "winner": { "id": 700001, "name": "Max Verstappen", … } } ] } }
GET

/v2/races/{id}/results

The race’s classification — motorsport: the main race session’s (the last session of type race: grid, pit stops, tyres, best laps, points; meta.session names it); a cycling stage race: the general classification, with each rider’s side classifications (points, mountains, young rider, jersey) — or, with session=, one session’s (a practice, qualifying, a stage) or one qualifying part’s (Q1, Q2…). A knock-out qualifying the source keeps only per part (MotoGP) is assembled from its parts the way the series ranks it: the Q2 riders first in Q2 order, then the Q1 riders not promoted, in Q1 order, places continuing; each line names its part.

Parameters

id
pathrequired
our numeric id (positive integer)
session
query
a session id from /v2/races/{id}, or a qualifying part id from its sessions[].parts
data
RaceResult[]
meta
race, session (the one read — the main race session in motorsport when none is asked for; null = the race’s own table), count
errors
400 bad_request — invalid session403 history_not_in_plan — the race started before your plan’s history404 not_found — not a race id, or a session of another race404 no_data — a duplicate copy under a second series (as /v2/races/{id}; error.series / error.race point to the real ones)
state is classified, didNotFinish, didNotStart, disqualified or notClassified; position is null for a competitor out of the classification (the source can also leave a place out). timeMs is the total time (race, stage) or the best lap (practice, qualifying); timeMs, gapMs and intervalMs are null for the lapped (see lapsBehind) and the out, and for a classified rider the source recorded no time for (cycling). tyreStints: Formula 1 races only; cycling is null outside a stage race’s overall result. part ("Q2", "Q1") is set only on a qualifying assembled from its parts: timeMs / gapMs / intervalMs are then that part’s (best lap, gap to that part’s fastest); a line without a time has position null; while a part is not finished its entrants hold its places (during Q2 the riders out in Q1 rank 13th onwards). Formula 1 qualifying has its own table and part null.
cURLTry it →
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" \
    "https://api.sportsapi.app/v2/races/{id}/results"
Example
{ "data": [ …,
    { "position": 2, "competitor": { "id": 700002, "name": "Charles Leclerc", … }, "team": { "id": 700010, "name": "Ferrari", … },
      "state": "classified", "outReason": null, "carNumber": 16, "gridPosition": 2, "startedFromPitLane": false,
      "laps": 62, "lapsBehind": null, "lapsLed": null, "pitStops": 2, "timeMs": 6128120, "gapMs": 7335, "intervalMs": 7335,
      "bestLapMs": 95202, "bestLapNumber": 41, "fastestLap": true, "points": 18,
      "tyreStints": [ { "compound": "soft", "laps": 24 }, { "compound": "medium", "laps": 15 }, { "compound": "soft", "laps": 23 } ],
      "cycling": null }, … ],
  "meta": { "race": 812345, "session": null, "count": 20 } }

// Cycling stage race (general classification):
    { "position": 1, "competitor": { "name": "Tadej Pogačar", … }, "team": { "name": "UAE Team Emirates", … }, "state": "classified",
      "timeMs": 266186000, "gapMs": null, …, "tyreStints": [],
      "cycling": { "jersey": "general", "pointsPosition": 2, "points": 289, "mountainsPosition": 1, "mountainsPoints": 154,
                   "youngRiderPosition": null, "youngRiderTimeMs": null } }

/v2/series/{id}/standings

The championship table of a season: the drivers’ / riders’ (type=competitors, default) or the teams’ (type=teams) — points, wins, podiums, pole positions, fastest laps, races started and races with points.

Parameters

id
pathrequired

season
query
a season id from /v2/series/{id}/seasons (default: the newest)
type
query
competitors (default) | teams
data

meta

errors

Cycling has no teams table (an empty array). team is null in the teams’ table. Columns the source does not keep are null. meta.figuresSource says where wins / podiums / polePositions / racesStarted / racesWithPoints come from: upstream (the source’s table) or computed — MotoGP, whose table has positions and points only: we count them from the main race of each finished round (win = 1st, podium = top 3, pole = grid 1; sprints not counted; a team counts each of its entries, one start per race). fastestLaps stays null for MotoGP.

    "points": 545, "wins": 11, "podiums": 15, "polePositions": 8, "fastestLaps": null, "racesStarted": 17, "racesWithPoints": 16 }, … ],
  "meta": { "season": 696722, "type": "competitors", "count": 32, "figuresSource": "computed" } }

Parameters

q
queryrequired
the search text: 2–100 characters after trimming, no control characters (a 400 names q otherwise)
data
SearchResult[]
meta
query, count
errors
400 bad_request — missing query
Tennis players and other individual-sport competitors come back as type team (in this API a competitor is a team). type is a closed set that grew on 2026-10-24 (manager, referee, series, race): skip a value you do not know. image is null for managers, referees, series and races.
