Site & account

Endpoints the sportsapi.app site uses. They take no API key (CORS-enabled like the rest of the API) and do not count against any quota.

GET

/captcha

A fresh 4-character image captcha: an SVG data URI to show in an <img>, and its id. Send the id and what the user typed as captchaId + captchaAnswer. Each captcha is good for ONE attempt, right or wrong, and for 5 minutes; answers are not case-sensitive.

data
{ id: string; image: string; expiresInSeconds: number }
errors
429 rate_limited — 30 per 10 minutes per IP (Retry-After)
Required on POST /contact, and on POST /auth/login after 3 failed attempts. The image is drawn, not text — the answer is not in the markup.
Example
$ curl https://api.sportsapi.app/captcha

{ "data": { "id": "6f1c0d…", "image": "data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0…", "expiresInSeconds": 300 } }
GET

/status

The data behind sportsapi.app/status: the overall state, each component’s current state, its uptime over 24 hours, 7 and 90 days, a 90-day daily series, and the incidents of the last 30 days. Measured by our own checks once a minute (REST API, WebSocket, live feed, data fetching, media CDN, database, keys & rate limits) — no third-party monitor.

data
{ status: "operational" | "degraded" | "outage"; updatedAt; since: string | null; intervalSeconds; daily: { start: "YYYY-MM-DD"; days: 90 }; components: { id; name; description; status: "operational" | "degraded" | "outage" | "unknown"; checkedAt; latencyMs; detail; uptime: { "24h"; "7d"; "90d" }; dailyUptime: (number | null)[]; dailyFailed: number[] }[]; incidents: { component; name; startedAt; endedAt: string | null; durationSeconds }[] }
errors
503 status_unavailable — the history could not be read
Uptime is the share of passing checks in percent (null = no checks in that window); 7d and 90d are UTC calendar days ending today, 24h is rolling. History starts at since (2026-10-20). Recomputed at most every 30 seconds (Cache-Control: max-age=30).
Example
$ curl https://api.sportsapi.app/status

{ "data": { "status": "operational", "updatedAt": "2026-10-20T12:00:20.000Z", "since": "2026-10-20T11:00:00.000Z",
    "intervalSeconds": 60, "daily": { "start": "2026-07-23", "days": 90 },
    "components": [ { "id": "api", "name": "REST API", "status": "operational", "checkedAt": "2026-10-20T12:00:00.000Z",
        "latencyMs": 4, "detail": null, "uptime": { "24h": 100, "7d": 100, "90d": 100 },
        "dailyUptime": [null, …, 100], "dailyFailed": [0, …, 0] }, … ],
    "incidents": [] } }
GET

/showcase/fixtures

The data behind sportsapi.app/live: the featured football fixtures — live, today’s and those that kicked off in the last 24 hours — of the Premier League, LaLiga, Serie A, Bundesliga, Ligue 1, the Champions League, the Europa League, the Süper Lig and the Trendyol 1.Lig. The scoreboard, our model’s numbers and, while a match is live, its curve so far and the newest AI commentary line. No API key.

data
{ id; startTime; status: { type; phase; description; period }; league: { id; name; image } | null; home / away: { id; name; shortName; code; image } | null; homeScore; awayScore; homeRedCards; awayRedCards; clock: Clock | null; winProbability: { model; prematch: { home; draw; away } | null; current: { home; draw; away } | null } | null; curve: { minute; addedMinute; home; draw; away }[] | null; lastCommentary: { minute; addedMinute; kind; text } | null }[]
meta
count, leagues
Live first, then upcoming, then finished (newest first); at most 80. winProbability.prematch is the estimate before kick-off (fixed at kick-off), current the latest (the result once finished); curve (thinned, ≤ 60 points) and lastCommentary are set only while the match is live. Rebuilt at most every 30 seconds (Cache-Control: max-age=30). A showcase, not a data feed: for any fixture or league use the /v2 endpoints with a key.
Example
$ curl https://api.sportsapi.app/showcase/fixtures

{ "data": [ { "id": 236923, "startTime": "2026-10-18T13:00:00.000Z",
    "status": { "type": "inprogress", "phase": "inprogress", "description": "2nd half", "period": "period2" },
    "league": { "id": 195910, "name": "Serie A", "image": "https://cdn.sportsapi.app/v2/leagues/195910/logo" },
    "home": { "id": 1902, "name": "Fiorentina", "shortName": "Fiorentina", "code": "FIO", "image": "…" },
    "away": { "id": 1907, "name": "Como", "shortName": "Como", "code": "COM", "image": "…" },
    "homeScore": 1, "awayScore": 3, "homeRedCards": null, "awayRedCards": null, "clock": { … },
    "winProbability": { "model": "v3", "prematch": { "home": 0.48, "draw": 0.26, "away": 0.26 }, "current": { "home": 0.02, "draw": 0.07, "away": 0.91 } },
    "curve": [ { "minute": 0, "addedMinute": null, "home": 0.48, "draw": 0.26, "away": 0.26 }, … ],
    "lastCommentary": { "minute": 71, "addedMinute": null, "kind": "goal", "text": "…" } }, … ],
  "meta": { "count": 12, "leagues": 8 } }
GET

/showcase/fixtures/{id}

The data behind sportsapi.app/match/{id} for a FEATURED fixture: the fixture, its events (oldest first), our win probability (pre-match, current and the curve), the AI commentary (oldest first) and a few key statistics (keys as in /statistics: ballPossession, totalShots, bigChances, …). No API key.

Parameters

id
pathrequired
our numeric id (positive integer)
data
{ fixture: Fixture; events: Incident[]; winProbability: WinProbability | null; commentary: CommentaryEntry[]; keyStats: { key; name; home; away }[] }
meta
refreshSeconds, commentary
errors
404 not_found — not a featured fixture (any fixture outside /showcase/fixtures)
Rebuilt at most every 10 seconds and shared by every viewer (Cache-Control: max-age=10) — the site polls it. Following a live or just-finished match keeps its commentary being written.
Example
$ curl https://api.sportsapi.app/showcase/fixtures/236923

{ "data": { "fixture": { "id": 236923, "sport": "football", … }, "events": [ … ],
    "winProbability": { "fixtureId": 236923, "model": "v3", "current": { "home": 0.0412, "draw": 0.0854, "away": 0.8734, … }, "series": [ … ], … },
    "commentary": [ …, { "seq": 4, "kind": "goal", "minute": 56, "text": "…", … } ],
    "keyStats": [ { "key": "ballPossession", "name": "Possession", "home": "47%", "away": "53%" }, … ] },
  "meta": { "refreshSeconds": 10, "commentary": "claude" } }
POST

/contact

Send a message through the contact form. JSON body: name (1–100 chars), email, company (optional, up to 120), message (10–5000 chars), captchaId + captchaAnswer (from GET /captcha).

data
{ ok: true }
errors
400 bad_request — a field missing or out of range400 captcha_invalid — the captcha is missing, wrong, expired or already used: fetch a new one429 rate_limited — 5 per hour per IP, 3 per day per email (Retry-After)
Answers 201 Created. The form’s hidden website field must stay empty.
Example
$ curl -X POST https://api.sportsapi.app/contact -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{ "name": "Ada", "email": "[email protected]", "company": "Acme", "message": "We would like a quote for the Business plan.",
          "captchaId": "6f1c0d…", "captchaAnswer": "K7MX" }'

{ "data": { "ok": true } }
POST

/auth/login

Dashboard sign-in for accounts created with a password. JSON body: email, password — plus captchaId + captchaAnswer once a captcha is required. Returns a session token for the dashboard API (not an API key): 7 days, renewed by GET /account past half its life.

data
{ token: string; account: { id, email, plan } }
errors
401 invalid_credentials — wrong email or password; error.captchaRequired tells whether the next attempt needs a captcha400 captcha_required — 3 failed attempts from this IP or for this email in 10 minutes: send a captcha400 captcha_invalid — the captcha was wrong, expired or used: fetch a new one (the password was not checked)429 rate_limited — 30 per 10 minutes per IP, 10 per email (Retry-After)
A successful sign-in clears the failure count. POST /auth/logout ends nothing on the server — the client drops its token; POST /account/sessions/revoke-all (with the session token) signs out every browser.
Example
{ "error": { "code": "invalid_credentials", "message": "wrong email or password", "captchaRequired": true } }
POST

/auth/logout

Sign out of this browser. Sessions are stateless tokens, so this changes nothing on the server: discard the token. No body, no token needed.

data
{ ok: true }
Example
{ "data": { "ok": true } }
POST

/account/sessions/revoke-all

Sign out everywhere: every dashboard session of the account stops working at once, the calling one included. API keys are not affected. Needs the session token (Authorization: Bearer <session token>).

data
{ revoked: true }
errors
401 unauthorized | session_revoked | account_suspended — no valid session
Example
{ "data": { "revoked": true } }
GET

/auth/{google|github}/start

Sign in — or create an account — with Google or GitHub. A browser navigation, not an XHR: it redirects to the provider, then back to sportsapi.app/auth/callback.

Parameters

next
query
a site path to land on afterwards, e.g. /dashboard
tz
query
the visitor’s IANA time zone, e.g. Europe/Istanbul (recorded on a new account)
lang
query
the visitor’s BCP 47 language tag, e.g. en-US (recorded on a new account)
The only way to create an account. An invalid next, tz or lang is ignored, never an error.
Example
https://api.sportsapi.app/auth/google/start?next=/dashboard&tz=Europe/Istanbul&lang=tr-TR
POST

/auth/signup

Closed: new accounts are created with Google or GitHub sign-in. Existing accounts still log in with email and password (POST /auth/login).

errors
410 password_signup_closed
Example
{ "error": { "code": "password_signup_closed",
    "message": "New accounts are created with Google or GitHub sign-in (GET /auth/google/start or /auth/github/start). Existing accounts can still log in with their password." } }

WebSocket

Business plan · Full grade

Real-time score and status deltas. Mint a single-use ticket over REST, then connect — your API key never goes into a WebSocket URL. Business plan (Full grade) only — up to five concurrent connections per account.

POST

/v2/stream/ticket

Mint a single-use connection ticket, valid for 30 seconds. Authenticated, rate-limited and counted like any other /v2 call. No request body.

data
{ ticket: string; url: string; expiresInSeconds: number }
errors
403 ws_not_available — your plan has no WebSocket access
ExampleTry it →
$ curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…" https://api.sportsapi.app/v2/stream/ticket

{ "data": { "ticket": "8373e1…", "url": "wss://api.sportsapi.app/?ticket=8373e1…", "expiresInSeconds": 30 } }
WS

wss://api.sportsapi.app/?ticket={ticket}

Connect to the url from the ticket. The server greets you with a welcome frame (protocol 4 since 2026-10-23; 3 earlier that day, 2 from 2026-10-19); then subscribe to channels. A subscription starts with a snapshot (or, after a lastSeq replay or a repeated subscribe, a subscribed frame), followed by frames carrying a per-channel seq that increases by one per frame — an opaque number (it starts from the server clock, not 0). On livescores, sport:{slug} and league:{id} a fixture that enters the channel’s set (it kicks off, or the server first sees it) arrives as a fixture frame with the whole Fixture; deltas then patch it, and only fixtures you were given are patched — a fixture that leaves (finished, canceled) gets one last delta saying so.

Protocol 4: handle the fixture frame — a client that skips it misses every match that kicks off while it is connected. A delta’s changes are a partial Fixture: merge them key by key into what you hold (nested objects such as homeScore, clock and cricket innings merge too — they never replace the whole object). Every frame carries ts (server time, Unix ms). Close codes: 1008 invalid or expired ticket (mint a new one) — or, on an open connection, its API key was revoked, the account suspended or the plan changed (the reason says which; checked at once on those events and every minute), 1013 your plan’s concurrent-connection limit is reached. The server sends a protocol ping every heartbeatMs — connections that stop answering are dropped. A score that goes DOWN (a disallowed goal, a corrected basket) arrives up to 1.5 s after the source sends it (football: 5 s), together with its lowered period scores: the source sometimes re-sends an older score for a moment, and such flaps are dropped (since 2026-10-24).
Frame flowOpen tester →
← { "type": "welcome", "protocol": 4, "heartbeatMs": 30000, "maxChannels": 50, "replay": true }
→ { "type": "subscribe", "channel": "livescores" }
← { "type": "snapshot", "channel": "livescores", "seq": 1760800000000, "ts": 1760800000000, "data": [ Fixture, … ] }
← { "type": "fixture", "channel": "livescores", "seq": 1760800000001, "ts": 1760800002480,
    "id": 201330, "sport": "basketball", "data": { "id": 201330, "sport": "basketball",
    "status": { "type": "inprogress", "phase": "inprogress", "code": 13, "description": "1st quarter", "period": "period1", "finish": null }, … } }
← { "type": "delta", "channel": "livescores", "seq": 1760800000002, "ts": 1760800004120,
    "id": 201324, "sport": "football",
    "changes": { "awayScore": { "current": 1, "periods": { "period2": 1 } } } }
← { "type": "delta", "channel": "livescores", "seq": 1760800000003, "ts": 1760800009310,
    "id": 201324, "sport": "football",
    "changes": { "status": { "code": 100, "description": "Ended", "type": "finished", "phase": "finished",
                             "finish": "regular", "period": null },
                 "winner": "away", "clock": null } }

// Reconnect with the last seq you hold (Business): the missed frames, then subscribed
→ { "type": "subscribe", "channel": "livescores", "lastSeq": 1760800000003 }
← { "type": "subscribed", "channel": "livescores", "seq": 1760800000003, "ts": 1760800030000, "replayed": 0 }

// fixture:{id} — play by play appended from index start (since 2026-10-24)
← { "type": "playByPlay", "channel": "fixture:201330", "seq": 1760800040000, "ts": 1760800041900, "id": 201330, "sport": "basketball",
    "start": 117, "total": 118, "entries": [ { "type": "scoreChange", "side": "home", "period": "period3", "periodSecond": 401,
      "text": "Jump shot made", "homeScore": 69, "awayScore": 74, "scoreType": "twoPointer", … } ] }
← { "type": "shotmap", "channel": "fixture:201324", "seq": 1760800050000, "ts": 1760800050500, "id": 201324, "sport": "football",
    "shots": [ { "side": "away", "outcome": "goal", "minute": 37, "period": "period1", … }, … ] }

→ { "type": "subscribe", "channel": "fixture:999999999999" }
← { "type": "error", "code": "unknown_fixture", "channel": "fixture:999999999999", "message": "no fixture with that id", "ts": 1760800031000 }
→ { "type": "unsubscribe", "channel": "sport:tennis" }
← { "type": "error", "code": "not_subscribed", "channel": "sport:tennis", "message": "not subscribed to this channel", "ts": 1760800032000 }

Channels

ChannelGradeSnapshotUpdates
livescoresFullFixture[] — every in-progress fixturefixture frames (id, sport, data: Fixture) when a fixture enters; deltas (id, sport, changes) for the fixtures you hold
sport:{slug}FullFixture[] — that sport’s in-progress fixturesfixture frames when a fixture enters; deltas (id, sport, changes) for the fixtures you hold
fixture:{id}FullFixture, or null if unavailable (an id we never issued → error unknown_fixture, not counted toward maxChannels)id, sport, changes — plus, while the fixture is in play: events frames (id, sport, events: the whole keyed list, changes: added / updated / removed) when its match events change, statistics frames (id, sport, statistics) and lineups frames (id, sport, lineups) when those change — fetched from REST (the live feed carries none of them): events ~20 s and ~45 s after each score / red-card / status change and every 30 s, statistics and lineups every 30 s, pushed only on a change. Since 2026-10-24 also playByPlay frames (id, sport, start, total, entries: the list from index start on — keep your first start entries and append; start beyond what you hold → reread REST; football and basketball, polled every 20 s), momentum frames (id, sport, momentum: the whole object) and shotmap frames (id, sport, shots: the whole list) — football, every 30 s; pushed only on a change, to at most 20 subscribed fixtures at once (the most-subscribed). For football also winProbability frames (id, sport, model, point) when an outcome moves ≥ 1 pp, and commentary frames (id, sport, entry) for each new AI commentary entry
league:{id}FullFixture[] — that league’s in-progress fixtures (our league id; unknown id → error unknown_league)fixture frames when a fixture enters; deltas (id, sport, changes) for the fixtures you hold
race:{id}FullRaceSnapshot — { race: Race, session, results: RaceResult[] }: the race with its sessions, the session running (else the last finished) and its classification (an id that is no race → error unknown_race)race frames (id, sport, data: Race) when a session starts / ends or the race changes, and raceResults frames (id, sport, session, results) when the running session’s classification changes — polled from REST (race sports have no live feed): the race every 60 s while a session runs or starts within 15 min, results every 30 s, pushed only on a change

Client frames

{ "type": "subscribe", "channel": "…", "lastSeq"?: n }

Start a channel; answered with a snapshot. On the Full grade, passing the last seq you hold replays the missed frames instead, then a { "type": "subscribed", "channel", "seq", "ts", "replayed" } frame (the server keeps 5 minutes of frames per channel; older gaps get a fresh snapshot). A subscribe to a channel you are already on is answered with subscribed (replayed 0).

{ "type": "unsubscribe", "channel": "…" }

Stop a channel; answered with { "type": "unsubscribed", "channel", "ts" } — or error not_subscribed when you are not on it.

{ "type": "resync", "channel": "…" }

Request a fresh snapshot of a channel you are subscribed to (error not_subscribed otherwise).

{ "type": "ping" }

Application-level ping; answered with { "type": "pong", "ts": <ms> }.

Close codes

1008invalid, expired or already used ticket — mint a new one; on an open connection: the API key was revoked, the account suspended, or the plan no longer includes this WebSocket grade (reason “plan changed; reconnect” = reconnect with a new ticket)
1013your plan’s concurrent-connection limit is reached — close another connection, retry later

WsErrorCode

WebSocket error code.

bad_frameThe frame was not valid JSON, not a known shape, or lacks a field it needs (`message` names the field, e.g. "channel: required").
unknown_channelNot a channel name we serve (or an unknown sport slug).
channel_forbiddenThe channel is not in your plan’s grade.
unknown_leagueleague:{id} names a league id we never issued (use the ids of /v2/leagues and of fixtures’ league) — REST answers the same id with 404 not_found.
unknown_fixturefixture:{id} names a fixture id we never issued — REST answers the same id with 404 not_found. The channel is not counted.
unknown_racerace:{id} names no race (a season or session id, or one we never issued) — /v2/races/{id} answers the same id with 404. The channel is not counted.
not_subscribedresync / unsubscribe of a channel this connection is not on.
too_many_channelsYou hit maxChannels on this connection.
snapshot_failedThe snapshot could not be built — send resync to retry (for league:{id}, when the league id could not be checked right now: subscribe again).
rate_limitedMore than 60 frames in 10 seconds on this connection; frames are dropped until the window resets.
Reconnecting: mint a fresh ticket each time (tickets are single-use). Apply deltas to the snapshot you hold; if a seq is skipped, send resync, or on the Full grade resubscribe with lastSeq to replay the gap.

Server frames

Every frame the server sends, field by field. A delta's changes is a FixturePatch: deep-merge it onto the Fixture you hold. A fixture frame adds a Fixture to a list channel.

WsWelcome

First frame after connecting.

FieldTypeMeaning
type"welcome"
protocolintegerProtocol version — 4 since 2026-10-23 evening (a fixture entering a list channel arrives as a `fixture` frame); 3 from 2026-10-23, 2 from 2026-10-19.
heartbeatMsintegerThe server pings this often; answer pings (the browser does) or be dropped.
maxChannelsintegerChannels allowed on this connection.
replaybooleanWhether `lastSeq` replay is available on your plan.

WsSnapshot

Full state of a channel: sent on subscribe and on resync.

FieldTypeMeaning
type"snapshot"
channelstring
seqintegerThe channel’s current sequence number. Opaque and increasing — not 0-based; the next delta has seq + 1.
tsintegerServer time, Unix milliseconds.
dataFixture[] | Fixture | RaceSnapshot | nulllivescores / sport:{slug} / league:{id}: Fixture[] (league: that league’s in-progress fixtures); fixture:{id}: Fixture, or null if unavailable; race:{id}: RaceSnapshot, or null if unavailable.

WsDelta

One fixture changed. On livescores / sport:{slug} / league:{id} a delta only names a fixture the channel already gave you (in its snapshot or a `fixture` frame); a fixture that leaves the channel (finished, canceled) gets one last delta saying so. Deltas carry live-feed changes and the corrections a board refresh makes; a score that goes DOWN (a disallowed goal, a corrected basket) arrives up to 1.5 s after the source sends it — the source sometimes re-sends an older score for a moment, and such flaps are dropped; a REST refetch of /fixtures/{id} can still be a few seconds newer — resync now and then if you need it exact.

FieldTypeMeaning
type"delta"
channelstring
seqintegerPrevious seq + 1 on this channel; a gap means a delta was lost — send resync.
tsintegerServer time, Unix milliseconds.
idintegerOur fixture id.
sportstringSport slug of the fixture.
changesFixturePatchThe `changes` of a WebSocket delta: a partial Fixture with the same names and nesting. Deep-merge it onto the Fixture you hold — objects merge key by key, any other value (null included) replaces. Only these fields are ever sent.

WsFixture

livescores / sport:{slug} / league:{id}: a fixture entered the channel’s set (it kicked off, or the server first saw it) — the whole Fixture, as a snapshot would hold it. Add it to your list; later deltas patch it. Not sent on fixture:{id} channels.

FieldTypeMeaning
type"fixture"
channelstring
seqintegerPrevious seq + 1 on this channel (shared with the deltas).
tsintegerServer time, Unix milliseconds.
idintegerOur fixture id.
sportstringSport slug of the fixture.
dataFixtureA match. The same object on every endpoint and in WebSocket snapshots.

WsSubscribed

Confirms a subscribe that did not send a snapshot: a `lastSeq` replay (after the replayed frames), or a second subscribe to a channel you are already on.

FieldTypeMeaning
type"subscribed"
channelstring
seqintegerThe channel’s current seq after the replay — the next delta has seq + 1.
tsintegerServer time, Unix milliseconds.
replayedintegerHow many frames the replay sent (0 = nothing was missed, or a subscribe to a channel you are already on).

WsWinProbability

fixture:{id} channels of in-play football fixtures: the win-probability estimate moved by at least one percentage point (checked on every change of the fixture and once a minute). `point` is the endpoint’s `current` (with the reason it moved) and `point.at` is when it was computed — NOT a point of the stored curve, whose minute points sit at minute ends: build a chart from GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/win-probability and keep it current with `?since=`.

FieldTypeMeaning
type"winProbability"
channelstring
seqintegerPrevious seq + 1 on this channel (shared with the channel’s deltas).
tsintegerServer time, Unix milliseconds.
idintegerOur fixture id.
sport"football"Sport slug of the fixture (win probability is football only).
modelWinProbabilityModelModel version (the docs describe each). A new version is announced in the changelog.
pointWinProbabilityPointA point of the win-probability curve: an estimate and why it was emitted.

WsCommentary

fixture:{id} channels of football fixtures: a new AI commentary entry was written. The frame’s `seq` is the channel’s (shared with the deltas); `entry.seq` is the entry’s number in GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/commentary — two different counters.

FieldTypeMeaning
type"commentary"
channelstring
seqintegerPrevious seq + 1 on this channel (shared with the channel’s deltas).
tsintegerServer time, Unix milliseconds.
idintegerOur fixture id.
sport"football"Sport slug of the fixture (commentary is football only).
entryCommentaryEntryOne AI commentary entry.

WsEvents

fixture:{id} channels of fixtures in play: the match events changed (goal, card, substitution, VAR decision, period, …). Fetched from REST by the server — the live feed carries no events: refetched about 20 s and 45 s after each score, red-card or status change (the source lists a goal 18–33 s after the score moves) and every 30 s while in play (cards and substitutions have no signal). Sent only when the list changed; a goal that is chalked off arrives in `changes.removed`, never before REST confirms it. The list is whole, so a missed frame costs nothing; before the first one, read GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/events.

FieldTypeMeaning
type"events"
channelstring
seqintegerPrevious seq + 1 on this channel (shared with the channel’s deltas).
tsintegerServer time, Unix milliseconds.
idintegerOur fixture id.
sportstringSport slug of the fixture.
eventsKeyedIncident[]The WHOLE events list now, oldest first — the same incidents as GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/events, each with its key. Replace your copy with it.
changesIncidentChangesWhat an events frame changed against the previous one.

WsStatistics

fixture:{id} channels of fixtures in play: the match statistics changed — the whole object, as GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/statistics. Polled from REST every 30 s while someone is subscribed (plus once after full time); sent only when the content changed. Expect ~30–60 s behind the pitch.

FieldTypeMeaning
type"statistics"
channelstring
seqintegerPrevious seq + 1 on this channel (shared with the channel’s deltas).
tsintegerServer time, Unix milliseconds.
idintegerOur fixture id.
sportstringSport slug of the fixture.
statisticsStatisticsMatch statistics, per period.

WsLineups

fixture:{id} channels of fixtures in play: the lineups changed — the whole object, as GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/lineups (per-player statistics included). Polled every 30 s while subscribed until they are confirmed and unchanged for 10 minutes; substitutions arrive as events.

FieldTypeMeaning
type"lineups"
channelstring
seqintegerPrevious seq + 1 on this channel (shared with the channel’s deltas).
tsintegerServer time, Unix milliseconds.
idintegerOur fixture id.
sportstringSport slug of the fixture.
lineupsLineupsLineups of both sides.

WsPlayByPlay

fixture:{id} channels of football and basketball fixtures in play: the source’s play by play (text commentary) changed. Polled from REST every 20 s while someone is subscribed (the source’s own page re-polls every 15–20 s), plus once after full time; sent only when the list changed, from the first changed entry on. Before the first frame, read GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/play-by-play.

FieldTypeMeaning
type"playByPlay"
channelstring
seqintegerPrevious seq + 1 on this channel (shared with the channel’s deltas).
tsintegerServer time, Unix milliseconds.
idintegerOur fixture id.
sportstringSport slug of the fixture.
startintegerIndex (0-based) in the whole list of the first entry in `entries`. Keep your first `start` entries, drop the rest, append `entries`. Usually your list’s length (new lines appended); smaller when the source corrected or removed a line.
totalintegerLength of the whole list now (= start + entries.length). Your list is out of step when `start` is beyond its length — read GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/play-by-play again.
entriesPlayByPlayEntry[]The entries from `start` on, oldest first, as GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/play-by-play lists them.

WsMomentum

fixture:{id} channels of football fixtures in play: the momentum graph changed — the whole object, as GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/momentum (one point per minute, so about once a minute). Polled every 30 s while subscribed, plus once after full time; sent only when it changed.

FieldTypeMeaning
type"momentum"
channelstring
seqintegerPrevious seq + 1 on this channel (shared with the channel’s deltas).
tsintegerServer time, Unix milliseconds.
idintegerOur fixture id.
sportstringSport slug of the fixture.
momentumMomentumMomentum graph: per minute (football, basketball, handball, ice hockey, …) or per game (tennis).

WsShotmap

fixture:{id} channels of football fixtures in play: the shot map changed (a new shot, or the source corrected one). Polled every 30 s while subscribed, plus once after full time; sent only when it changed. Expect ~30–60 s behind the pitch.

WsRace

Changelog

Breaking changes to the data contract, newest first, with what a field was called before and what it is now.

2026-10-28breaking

Monthly request quotas on paid plans

Breaking (quota window): Starter, Pro and Business now count requests per UTC calendar month instead of per UTC day, at 30 times the old daily figure, so a busy match weekend no longer runs into a daily cap. Free stays 100 a day. One set of limit headers: RateLimit-Limit / -Remaining / -Reset now describe the quota (they described the per-minute window before); the per-minute limits themselves are unchanged and report themselves only through a 429 rate_limited with Retry-After. WebSocket protocol unchanged (4).

WhatBeforeNow
Starter quota25,000 requests per UTC day750,000 requests per UTC month (resets 00:00 UTC on the 1st)
Pro quota150,000 requests per UTC day4,500,000 requests per UTC month
Business quota3,000,000 requests per UTC day90,000,000 requests per UTC month
Free quota100 requests per UTC dayunchanged: 100 requests per UTC day
Requests already made this month—count toward the first monthly quota: October 2026 starts from what each account used since 2026-10-01
429 quota_exceededmessage “daily quota exceeded”; Retry-After = seconds until 00:00 UTCmessage names the period and the reset (“monthly quota exceeded (750000 requests per UTC month); it resets at 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z”); Retry-After = seconds until the reset — up to a month on paid plans
Response headersRateLimit-Limit / -Remaining / -Reset for the minute window; nothing for the quotaRateLimit-Limit = the quota (requests per month, or per day on Free), RateLimit-Remaining = requests left in it, RateLimit-Reset = seconds until it resets; no header for the minute window. (Quota-Limit / -Remaining / -Reset / -Period, sent for a few hours on 2026-10-28, are gone — one set of headers.)
Per-minute rate limits10 / 300 / 600 / 6,000 a minuteunchanged; a 429 rate_limited names the limit (“rate limit exceeded (300 requests per minute)”) and Retry-After is the seconds to the next minute
2026-10-28

Freshness only, no shape change: esports period scores follow the source within about 15 seconds on a watched fixture, and squads / profiles of teams you read follow a transfer within about a day. WebSocket protocol unchanged (4).

New endpoints, race sports and WebSocket protocol 4

Breaking for WebSocket clients only (protocol 4): on livescores, sport:{slug} and league:{id} a fixture that enters the channel now arrives as a new fixture frame carrying the whole Fixture, and deltas name only fixtures the channel gave you — a client that skips unknown frame types would miss every match that kicks off while it is connected. Everything else is additive: motorsport and cycling (races, sessions, results, series standings), rankings, a league directory, team competitions, a season player-statistics explorer, play-by-play, head-to-head fixtures, knockout brackets, new Fixture fields (referee, managers, tennis surface and serving, cricket toss and umpires, previous leg, fight card), goal build-ups, player injuries, tennis player profiles, and data for more sports on shot map, best players, momentum and point by point. Nothing was renamed or removed.

Schema overhaul: one vocabulary across sports

Breaking. Statistic keys are now one vocabulary across sports and between match, player and season statistics; extra time moved into the score’s periods; events, shot map and commentary are oldest first; meta counts are named <noun>Count; standings default to type overall with a new primary flag; several enum values and fields were renamed. A client must update the keys it reads (the full per-sport statistic key table is in the reference), reverse any newest-first assumption, and read the new meta names. Stored data is served in the new shape — nothing is mixed. WebSocket protocol 3.

ScoreSide.extra1, extra2, overtimescalar fields on homeScore / awayScoreremoved — now inside periods: periods.extra1 / periods.extra2 (football, futsal), periods.overtime (every other sport; baseball only when the source gives no per-inning breakdown); football no longer repeats an overtime total (it was extra1 + extra2)

History depth by plan

Breaking for Free, Starter and Pro keys that read old data. Each plan now reaches back a set number of days: Free 7 days, Starter 3 months, Pro 12 months, Business the full history. Older fixtures, days and seasons answer 403 history_not_in_plan; fixture lists leave older fixtures out. Upcoming and live data are not limited. No response shape changed.

WhatBeforeNow
GET /v2/fixtures?date=any date from 1990a date before the plan’s history → 403 history_not_in_plan (error.historyFrom = first readable day)
GET /v2/fixtures/{id} and its sub-resourcesany fixturea fixture that kicked off before the plan’s history → 403 history_not_in_plan
League season endpoints, team / player season statisticsany seasona season that ended before the plan’s history → 403 history_not_in_plan
Team / player / round fixture listsevery fixturefixtures before the plan’s history left out; meta.historyFrom set and hasNextPage false when that happened

Win probability: model v2 pre-match

Additive. A new pre-match model (v2): each team’s strength now comes from its recent matches in all competitions, its domestic league table and our league-strength coefficients, so a cup or European tie between teams of different leagues — and the first games of a campaign — are judged on more than the competition’s own table. In play nothing changed. Fixtures whose pre-match estimate was fixed under v1 keep model v1. Nothing was renamed or removed.

WhatBeforeNow
WinProbability.model, WsWinProbability.model"v1""v1" or "v2" (enum WinProbabilityModel) — new estimates are v2
WinProbabilityPrematch{ home, draw, away, homeExpectedGoals, awayExpectedGoals, standings, form }also allCompetitions and domesticTables — whether the teams’ recent matches / domestic tables were available; null for model v1
2026-10-22

Win-probability history with time

Additive. Every win-probability estimate now carries the UTC instant it describes, the curve is kept as history (a point is stored once it is two minutes old and not changed after), and the endpoint takes ?since= for clients that poll. Nothing was renamed or removed.

WhatBeforeNow
WinProbabilityState / WinProbabilityPoint{ home, draw, away, minute, addedMinute, homeScore, awayScore (, reason) }also at — ISO-8601 UTC instant, non-decreasing along the series; null only for points stored before this change whose kick-off time is unknown
GET /v2/fixtures/{id}/win-probabilitythe whole curveoptional ?since=<ISO-8601 instant> → only the points after it (current always); meta.since echoes it; 400 bad_request for an invalid instant
WebSocket winProbability framepoint without a timepoint.at = when the estimate was computed; protocol version unchanged (2)

Behaviour only — no field, type or route changed. A squad or a player’s current team is refreshed on the next request once a move shows in a lineup, a squad, a profile or a transfers list, instead of waiting up to 30 hours. See Data freshness.

Moved fixtures corrected in every list, player fixtures refreshed on a reschedule

Behaviour only — no field, type or route changed. A fixture not yet started now shows its new start time or its postponement in every list as soon as we have seen it, and a player’s fixtures refresh when one of his matches is moved or postponed. See Data freshness.

Reschedules, postponements and player lists refreshed

Objects

Every object the API returns, field by field — generated from the same schemas the API validates its output against (also published as OpenAPI 3.1). Every field is always present: null when the source has no value, never absent (fields marked ? appear only in WebSocket patches). Units are in the field name or shown next to it; instants are ISO-8601 UTC, dates YYYY-MM-DD.

Fixture

A match. The same object on every endpoint and in WebSocket snapshots.

FieldTypeMeaning
idintegerOur fixture id.
sportstringSport slug (as in /v2/sports).
statusStatusMatch status.
startTimestring (ISO-8601 UTC) | nullStart time: the scheduled start, replaced by the recorded kick-off once the source records it (the live feed sends it a few minutes after the start). The same value on every endpoint and in WebSocket deltas.
leagueLeagueRef | nullThe competition. null when the source files the fixture under a competition it has no league for — seen on minor regional football (South Africa’s National Second Division, 2026-10-23); season and round are then null too.
seasonSeason | nullThe season.
roundRound | nullThe round, when the competition has rounds.
homeTeamRef | nullHome side; null while the side is not decided yet (the source’s placeholder such as "WQF1", winner of quarter-final 1).
awayTeamRef | nullAway side; null while the side is not decided yet (the source’s placeholder such as "WQF1").
homeScoreScoreSideOne side’s score.
awayScoreScoreSideOne side’s score.
winnerWinner | nullNull until status.type is finished, and for a fight ruled a no contest (`fightResult.method` noContest). A match finished on penalties: the shoot-out winner, whatever the source says (on a second leg the source names the side that won the 90 minutes). Named from the score when the source leaves it out, or calls a match draw in a sport that cannot draw (regular time or overtime finishes; not cricket).
venueVenue | nullVenue, when known (often null in lower tiers). Filled on /fixtures/{id} and, when the source lists it, in date lists; the source’s round, team, player and live lists carry no venue, so null there means "not included", not "unknown" — read /fixtures/{id} for it.
clockClock | nullMatch clock; null when the source has none for the fixture and once it is over.
firstToServeSide | nullDeprecated (2026-10-23): the same value as `serving`. The source updates this field every game / leg, so it is the side serving (throwing) NOW, not who served first — read `serving`.
servingSide | nullTennis / darts / other serve sports: the side serving (throwing) now, as the source updates it every game / leg. Null when the source does not say.
homeSeedstring | nullSeeded competitions — tennis draws, playoff seeding (basketball, …): the home side’s seed ("1", "12") or entry status ("WC" wild card, "Q" qualifier, "LL" lucky loser, "PR" protected ranking, …), as the draw prints it. Null when unseeded.
awaySeedstring | nullThe away side’s seed or entry status, like homeSeed.
notestring | nullCricket: the source’s match note — the result line once finished ("Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by 37 runs"). Display only.
battingSideSide | nullCricket: the side batting now. Null when no innings is in progress and for other sports.
fightResultFightResult | nullMMA / boxing: method, round and time of the finish. Null until status.type is finished, and when the source has no method.
fightDisciplineFightDiscipline | nullCombat sports (sport `mma`, which also carries boxing, kickboxing and Muay Thai cards): the discipline of this fight, when the source tags it. The source tags only some cards (ONE, Queensbury, some OKTAGON fights; not UFC or PFL), so null does not mean MMA.
refereeReferee | nullThe referee, when the source names one (football and some other sports; cricket: the match referee). Filled on /fixtures/{id}; lists carry null (not included).
homeManagerManagerRef | nullThe home side’s manager / head coach for this fixture, when the source names one. Filled on /fixtures/{id}; lists carry null.
awayManagerManagerRef | nullThe away side’s manager / head coach, like homeManager.
surfaceSurface | nullTennis: the court surface. Filled on /fixtures/{id} and live lists; null for other sports.
tossCricketToss | nullCricket: the toss, once made. Filled on /fixtures/{id}; null for other sports.
umpiresstring[] | nullCricket: the on-field umpires as the source names them (often with a country code: "Asif Yaqoob (PAK)"); null when not listed and for other sports.
tvUmpirestring | nullCricket: the TV (third) umpire, like umpires.
previousLegFixtureIdinteger | nullTwo-legged ties and playoff series: our id of the previous leg / game of the tie, when the source links it. Read /fixtures/{id} of it for the first-leg score.
aggregateWinnerSide | nullSecond leg of a two-legged tie: the side that went through, once finished — the source’s verdict, else read from `aggregated` (higher wins) or, level on aggregate, the shoot-out. Null otherwise, and on a level aggregate the source does not settle (an away-goals rule). `winner` is this match’s winner: on a second leg decided on penalties both name the shoot-out winner; otherwise the two can differ (a side can win the second leg and go out). Filled on /fixtures/{id}; lists and live snapshots may carry null (not included).
fightCardFightCard | nullMMA / boxing: card section, order and weight class of the bout, when the source lists them.
attendanceinteger | nullSpectators, when the source reports it (seen on NBA and MLB games, often only once the game is under way). Filled on /fixtures/{id}; lists carry null (not included).
matchFormatMatchFormat | nullDarts and esports: the match format (best of N sets / legs / games), when the source gives it; null for other sports.
inningStateInningState | nullBaseball: the game state in play (inning, half, balls, strikes, outs, runners on base). Null unless the game is in progress (or interrupted), and for other sports. Live: in WebSocket deltas.
timeoutsTimeouts | nullBasketball: timeouts left per side. Null unless the game is in progress (or interrupted), and when the source does not track them. Live: in WebSocket deltas.

Status

Match status.

FieldTypeMeaning
typeStatusTypeCoarse state: derived from `phase` (see the StatusPhase table).
phaseStatusPhaseFine state, derived from `code`.
codeinteger | nullThe source’s status code — the full table is in the data dictionary. `phase`, `period` and `finish` already decode it.
descriptionstring | nullEnglish label for display, from our status table (the data dictionary’s status codes), sport-aware: e.g. "2nd half", "Halftime", "After extra time" (football), "After overtime" (basketball, ice hockey, …), "After extra innings" (baseball), "After penalties", "1st innings" (cricket), "Coverage canceled". The source’s own text only for a code we do not know. Do not branch on it.
periodPeriodKey | nullThe period in play (or, during a break, the one just played). Null before the start and once over.
finishFinishType | nullHow the match was decided; null unless `type` is finished.

ScoreSide

One side’s score.

FieldTypeMeaning
currentnumber | nullThe score as a scoreboard shows it: goals, points, sets won (tennis / volleyball), runs (cricket, baseball), extra time / overtime included. A penalty shoot-out is NOT included — it is in `penalties` — except in ice hockey, whose scoring credits the shoot-out winner with one goal (3-3 after overtime → 3-4). Null before the start, and on a fixture whose coverage was canceled.
periodsRecord<PeriodKey, number>Score per period, keyed by PeriodKey: goals per half / quarter / period, games per set (tennis), points per set (volleyball, table tennis), runs per inning (baseball). Extra time is here too: `extra1` / `extra2` (football, futsal), `overtime` (basketball, ice hockey, handball, American football, water polo, …), `period10`… (baseball extra innings; `overtime` only when the source gives the extra-innings runs as a total). The values add up to `current` when the source’s breakdown is complete (it sometimes is not: some baseball leagues send no innings, a few futsal matches miss a half) — ice hockey after a shoot-out is one goal short by design (see `current`). Esports: one key per game (map), and what the source counts there depends on the title — Counter-Strike 1 for the side that won map N and 0 otherwise (maps not played 0, up to period5 in a best of 3), League of Legends the side’s kills in game N (so they do not add up to `current`, which counts games won); read /fixtures/{id}/games for each game’s winner and score. Empty when the source has none.
tieBreaksRecord<PeriodKey, number>Tennis: tie-break points of a set, keyed like `periods` (e.g. { "period2": 7 }).
normalTimenumber | nullScore at the end of regulation time, when the source gives it.
penaltiesnumber | nullPenalty shoot-out score (goals scored in the shoot-out). Ice hockey: 1 for the shoot-out winner and 0 for the loser — the goal `current` credits.
aggregatednumber | nullAggregate over a two-legged tie.
seriesnumber | nullPlayoff series: games won in the series so far (basketball, baseball, ice hockey, water polo).
pointstring | nullTennis: the current game score, "0" | "15" | "30" | "40" | "A" (tie-break points as numbers, "0"–"N"). Null unless play is in progress or interrupted.
redCardsinteger | nullFootball: red cards shown to the side (second yellows included).
inningsRecord<PeriodKey, CricketInnings>Cricket: the side’s innings, keyed inning1…N. Empty for other sports.
hitsinteger | nullBaseball: hits (the H of the R/H/E line).
errorsinteger | nullBaseball: errors (the E of the R/H/E line).

CricketInnings

One innings of a side in cricket.

FieldTypeMeaning
runsinteger | nullRuns scored.
wicketsinteger | nullWickets lost.
oversnumber | nullOvers bowled, cricket notation (49.5 = 49 overs and 5 balls).
runRatenumber | nullRuns per over.
targetRunRatenumber | nullRequired run rate to reach the target (chasing side).

Clock

The match clock. Running clock (football, rugby, …): elapsed = periodOffsetSeconds + (now − periodStartedAt); minute = floor(elapsed / 60) + 1; past periodEndSeconds show periodEndSeconds / 60 + "+" + the extra minutes. Only while status.phase is inprogress. Stop clock (basketball, handball, ice hockey, …): playedSeconds as of playedAt, ticking only while `running` is true. Set / map sports (tennis, table tennis, badminton, esports): only `periodStartedAt` (when the current set or map started), when the source sends it — often the whole clock is null. Every field is null when the source does not supply it for the sport; the whole clock is null when there is none and once the match is over. Lists other than /fixtures/{id} may carry fewer clock fields (the static ones such as periodLengthSeconds can be null there).

FieldTypeMeaning
periodStartedAtstring (ISO-8601 UTC) | nullWhen the current period’s clock started.
periodOffsetSecondsnumber | nullRunning clock: clock seconds already elapsed when the period started (football 2nd half: 2700).seconds
periodEndSecondsnumber | nullRunning clock: the clock second at which the period’s regulation time ends (football 1st half: 2700).seconds
maxExtraSecondsnumber | nullRunning clock: the most added time the source’s display allows beyond periodEndSeconds.seconds
injuryTimeMinutesnumber | nullAdded time announced for the period in play.minutes
playedSecondsnumber | nullStop clock: seconds played, as of `playedAt`.seconds
playedAtstring (ISO-8601 UTC) | nullWhen `playedSeconds` was read.
runningboolean | nullStop clock: whether the game clock is running.
runningUpdatedAtstring (ISO-8601 UTC) | nullWhen `running` was last updated.
periodLengthSecondsnumber | nullStop clock: regulation length of one period.seconds
overtimeLengthSecondsnumber | nullLength of one overtime period.seconds
periodCountinteger | nullNumber of regulation periods (combat sports: scheduled rounds).

methodFightMethodHow it was won.

Null for a decision (unanimous, split, majority, technical — draws by decision included): the fight was not stopped, and the source’s figure for it is unreliable.seconds

FixturePatch

The `changes` of a WebSocket delta: a partial Fixture with the same names and nesting. Deep-merge it onto the Fixture you hold — objects merge key by key, any other value (null included) replaces. Only these fields are ever sent.

FieldTypeMeaning
status?{ type?: StatusType; phase?: StatusPhase; code?: integer | null; description?: string | null; period?: PeriodKey | null; finish?: FinishType | null }The status fields that changed (a status change always re-sends type, phase, finish and, when known, period).
startTime?string (ISO-8601 UTC) | nullNew start time: a reschedule, or the recorded kick-off once the source records it (see Fixture.startTime).
winner?Winner | nullSet when the match finishes.
homeScore?ScoreSidePatchThe changed part of a ScoreSide.
awayScore?ScoreSidePatchThe changed part of a ScoreSide.
clock?{ periodStartedAt?: string (ISO-8601 UTC) | null; periodOffsetSeconds?: number | null; periodEndSeconds?: number | null; maxExtraSeconds?: number | null; injuryTimeMinutes?: number | null; playedSeconds?: number | null; playedAt?: string (ISO-8601 UTC) | null; running?: boolean | null; runningUpdatedAt?: string (ISO-8601 UTC) | null; periodLengthSeconds?: number | null; overtimeLengthSeconds?: number | null; periodCount?: integer | null } | nullnull = the match is over: drop the clock.
firstToServe?Side | nullDeprecated: the same value as `serving`.
serving?Side | nullThe side serving (throwing) now.
note?string | nullCricket: new match note.
battingSide?Side | nullCricket: the side now batting (null = none).
inningState?InningState | nullBaseball: the new game state, always sent whole; null = no longer in play.
timeouts?{ homeRemaining?: integer | null; awayRemaining?: integer | null; perTeam?: integer | null } | nullBasketball: the timeout counts that changed; null = no longer in play.
fightResult?FightResult | nullMMA / boxing: the method, round and time of the finish, sent whole once the source has it — usually in a delta after the finishing one (the source publishes it ~20–60 s after the winner).

ScoreSidePatch

The changed part of a ScoreSide.

FieldTypeMeaning
current?number | nullThe score as a scoreboard shows it: goals, points, sets won (tennis / volleyball), runs (cricket, baseball), extra time / overtime included. A penalty shoot-out is NOT included — it is in `penalties` — except in ice hockey, whose scoring credits the shoot-out winner with one goal (3-3 after overtime → 3-4). Null before the start, and on a fixture whose coverage was canceled.
normalTime?number | nullScore at the end of regulation time, when the source gives it.
penalties?number | nullPenalty shoot-out score (goals scored in the shoot-out). Ice hockey: 1 for the shoot-out winner and 0 for the loser — the goal `current` credits.
aggregated?number | nullAggregate over a two-legged tie.
series?number | nullPlayoff series: games won in the series so far (basketball, baseball, ice hockey, water polo).
point?string | nullTennis: the current game score, "0" | "15" | "30" | "40" | "A" (tie-break points as numbers, "0"–"N"). Null unless play is in progress or interrupted.
redCards?integer | nullFootball: red cards shown to the side (second yellows included).
hits?integer | nullBaseball: hits (the H of the R/H/E line).
errors?integer | nullBaseball: errors (the E of the R/H/E line).
periods?Record<PeriodKey, number | null>Only the periods that changed; null = the period was removed upstream (delete it).
tieBreaks?Record<PeriodKey, number | null>Only the tie-breaks that changed; null = removed.
innings?Record<PeriodKey, CricketInnings>Only the innings that changed; merge key by key (like periods) — an innings not named is unchanged.

Other rows: the period between the period rows around it (the source’s own value when it gives one); shoot-out kicks: penalties. Null only when it cannot be told (no period row yet and the sport’s period length unknown).

Null otherwise, and on a level aggregate the source does not settle (an away-goals rule). `winner` is this match’s winner: on a second leg decided on penalties both name the shoot-out winner; otherwise the two can differ (a side can win the second leg and go out). WinProbability

Our own in-play win-probability model for a football fixture (documented in the docs): pre-match expected goals (v2: from both teams’ recent matches in all competitions, their domestic tables and league-strength coefficients, blended with the competition’s table and form), then updated by time left, score, red cards and momentum. An analysis indicator — not betting advice; no bookmaker odds are used.

FieldTypeMeaning
fixtureIdintegerOur fixture id.
modelWinProbabilityModelModel version (the docs describe each). A new version is announced in the changelog.
updatedAtstring (ISO-8601 UTC)When this estimate was computed.
prematchWinProbabilityPrematchThe pre-match estimate and the inputs it was built from. Fixed once computed (it does not move when the table is updated after the match).
currentWinProbabilityStateThe latest estimate: the pre-match one before kick-off, certainty (1 / 0 / 0) once finished.
seriesWinProbabilityPoint[]The curve, oldest first (by `at`): a point at kick-off, one per match minute, and one right after every goal, red card, period start / end and big missed chance. Empty before kick-off. History: a point is stored once it is two minutes old (or the match is over) and is not changed after, so the curve shows what the model said at the time; kept for good. With `?since=` only the points after that instant.
inputs{ shotmap: boolean; momentum: boolean; events: boolean }Which live inputs the in-play estimate used.

WinProbabilityPrematch

The pre-match estimate and the inputs it was built from. Fixed once computed (it does not move when the table is updated after the match).

FieldTypeMeaning
homenumberPre-match probability of a home win, 0–1.ratio
drawnumberPre-match probability of a draw, 0–1.ratio
awaynumberPre-match probability of an away win, 0–1.ratio
homeExpectedGoalsnumberThe model’s expected goals for the home side over the whole match (λ home).
awayExpectedGoalsnumberThe model’s expected goals for the away side over the whole match (λ away).
standingsbooleanWhether the league table was available (attack / defence ratings); false = league or global averages were used.
formbooleanWhether the pre-match form guide was available.
allCompetitionsboolean | nullModel v2: whether the teams’ recent matches in all competitions were available (strength from up to their last 20 results, weighted by age and by the opponent’s strength). Null for model v1.
domesticTablesboolean | nullModel v2: whether the teams’ domestic league tables were available (for a cup or European match: their own leagues’ tables, put on one scale by our league-strength coefficients). Null for model v1.

WinProbabilityState

One estimate of the result: home / draw / away probabilities at a moment of the match.

FieldTypeMeaning
homenumberProbability that the home side ends the match ahead on the scoreboard, 0–1.ratio
drawnumberProbability that the match ends level on the scoreboard (a penalty shoot-out is not counted), 0–1. home + draw + away = 1.ratio
awaynumberProbability that the away side ends the match ahead on the scoreboard, 0–1.ratio
minuteinteger | nullMatch minute of the estimate, as incidents count it (a goal in the 23rd minute is minute 23; 45+2 is minute 45, addedMinute 2). Null before kick-off.minutes
addedMinuteinteger | nullMinutes into added time, else null.minutes
homeScoreinteger | nullHome goals at that moment. Null before kick-off.
awayScoreinteger | nullAway goals at that moment. Null before kick-off.
atstring (ISO-8601 UTC) | nullUTC instant of the estimate. A curve point: the moment of the match it describes (the end of that minute, the goal, the whistle) — measured from the match clock while it runs, else estimated from kick-off (15 min half-time). `current`: when it was computed (in play / before kick-off) or the end of the match (finished). Non-decreasing along the series. Null only for points stored before 2026-10-22 whose kick-off time is unknown.

FieldTypeMeaning

awaynumberProbability that the away side ends the match ahead on the scoreboard, 0–1.ratio
minuteinteger | nullMatch minute of the estimate, as incidents count it (a goal in the 23rd minute is minute 23; 45+2 is minute 45, addedMinute 2). Null before kick-off.minutes
addedMinuteinteger | nullMinutes into added time, else null.minutes
homeScoreinteger | nullHome goals at that moment. Null before kick-off.
awayScoreinteger | nullAway goals at that moment. Null before kick-off.
atstring (ISO-8601 UTC) | nullUTC instant of the estimate. A curve point: the moment of the match it describes (the end of that minute, the goal, the whistle) — measured from the match clock while it runs, else estimated from kick-off (15 min half-time). `current`: when it was computed (in play / before kick-off) or the end of the match (finished). Non-decreasing along the series. Null only for points stored before 2026-10-22 whose kick-off time is unknown.

Commentary

AI match commentary for a football fixture, generated by Claude (Anthropic) from our own data only: one short entry per goal, red card, missed penalty, VAR decision, period start / end, big chance and sustained momentum swing, plus half-time and full-time summaries. Written once and shared by every client.

FieldTypeMeaning
fixtureIdintegerOur fixture id.
entriesCommentaryEntry[]Oldest first (by `seq`), like every timeline list. Empty until something has been written — commentary is generated only while someone follows the match (this endpoint, the fixture:{id} channel or the public showcase), so a match nobody watched has none.

CommentaryEntry

seqintegerPosition in the fixture’s commentary: 1, 2, 3, … in the order written. Never reused.

addedMinuteinteger | nullMinutes into added time, else null.minutes
textstringOne or two English sentences (summaries: up to three), written by Claude from our own data of the match only — events, score, clock, statistics and our win-probability model. No betting language. Plain text.
modelstringThe Claude model that wrote it, e.g. "claude-sonnet-5-5".
createdAtstring (ISO-8601 UTC)When it was written.

Enums

Every closed value set, with what each value means. A value not listed here is never sent — when the source introduces one we do not classify yet, the field reads other (or null) until this list grows.

Side

A side of the fixture.

homeThe fixture’s home side.
awayThe fixture’s away side.

Winner

Result of a finished fixture.

homeHome side won.
awayAway side won.
drawDraw.

StatusType

Coarse match state — what to filter on.

notstartedNot started yet (scheduled, or its start is delayed).
inprogressBeing played — including breaks such as half-time and a fight awaiting its decision.
interruptedStopped mid-match (weather, crowd, …) and expected to resume.
willcontinueA multi-day match between days (cricket Tests: end of day N).
postponedMoved to a later date; the fixture keeps its id.
canceledWill not be played (canceled, abandoned, removed).
finishedOver, with a result.

StatusPhase

Finer match state — what a scoreboard shows.

notstartedScheduled, not started.
delayedPast its start time, start delayed.
inprogressA period is being played (status.period says which).
breakA scheduled pause inside the match: half-time, pause between sets, awaiting extra time or penalties, cricket lunch / tea / drinks.
awaitingResultPlay is over, the result is not announced yet (combat sports judges’ decision).
interruptedStopped unexpectedly, expected to resume.
suspendedSuspended by the organiser; may resume another day.
willcontinueA multi-day match between days.
postponedMoved to a later date.
canceledCanceled before it started, or removed.
abandonedStarted and called off without a result.
finishedOver — status.finish says how it was decided.

FinishType

How a finished match was decided.

regularDecided in regulation (also every set / frame / game sport’s normal finish).
overtimeDecided in overtime / extra time / extra innings (upstream “AET”).
penaltiesDecided by a penalty shoot-out (upstream “AP”).
goldenSetDecided by a golden set (volleyball).
walkoverAwarded without being played.
retiredOne side retired during the match (tennis).
defaultedOne side was defaulted / disqualified.

FightMethod

How a fight was won.

koKnockout.
tkoTechnical knockout (referee or doctor stoppage).
submissionSubmission.
unanimousDecisionJudges’ decision, all judges agreeing.
splitDecisionJudges’ decision, split.
majorityDecisionJudges’ decision by a majority: two judges for the winner and one scoring a draw — or, with `winner: "draw"`, a majority draw (two judges scoring a draw; real boxing capture 2026-10-19).
technicalDecisionDecision on the scorecards after a stoppage.
pointsDecisionBoxing: a points decision (the source’s PTS — scored by the referee alone, as in British small-hall bouts; a draw comes with `winner: "draw"`).
disqualificationDisqualification.
noContestNo contest.
otherA method not classified yet (the source’s code is logged).

The combat discipline of a fight.

mmaMixed martial arts.
boxingBoxing.
kickboxingKickboxing.
muayThaiMuay Thai.

otherA discipline not classified yet (the source’s value is logged).

Availability

Whether a missing player is ruled out or doubtful.

doubtfulMay miss this fixture.

MissingReason

Why a player is missing.

injuryInjured (`description` names it when known, e.g. "Hamstring Injury").
illnessIll.
suspensionSuspended (other than a card ban).
absentAbsent for another reason (personal, international duty, …).
yellowCardSuspensionBanned for accumulated yellow cards.

StatKind

How to read a statistic’s value and total.

value`value` is the number shown (57 for "57%", 2.04 for "2.04"); `total` is null.
ratio`value` successes out of `total` attempts ("33/53 (62%)" → 33 of 53; a percentage-only display such as "42%" is still value / total).
time`value` is seconds; `total` is the seconds available (the period length), e.g. time spent in the lead.

HigherIs

Whether more is better.

betterA higher value is good for that side (shots, possession).
worseA higher value is bad for that side (fouls, turnovers, errors).

IncidentType

What happened.

goalA score: goal, basket, try, touchdown, … (`detail` says which kind). Set sports (volleyball, table tennis, badminton) do not list points — their set ends are `period` rows.
cardA card shown to a player (or a team official).
substitutionA player change: playerIn replaces playerOut.
periodA period ended — only that: a period still being played has no row (since 2026-10-23). `period` names the period that ended, `text` is the scoreboard label (HT, FT, Q2, 3rd period, 2. set, …). The scores are the running match score at that moment; in set sports (volleyball, table tennis, badminton) the sets won so far (the set’s own points are in the fixture’s `periods` and in /points).
injuryTimeAdded time announced: `addedMinute` minutes after `minute`.
varDecisionA video-review decision (`detail`), `confirmed` = the original call stood.
inGamePenaltyA penalty kick during play that did not produce a goal (`detail` missed); a scored one is a `goal` with detail `penalty`.
shootoutPenaltyOne kick of a penalty shoot-out: `shootoutSequence` = the overall kick order (1, 2, 3, … both sides counted), `shootoutRound` = the round (the taker’s side’s 1st, 2nd, … kick).
suspensionA timed exclusion (ice hockey penalty, handball two minutes): `durationSeconds`, `reason`.

IncidentDetail

The kind of incident within its type.

regulargoal: an ordinary goal; substitution: a tactical change.
ownGoalgoal: scored by the conceding side (`side` = the team credited with the goal).
penaltygoal: a penalty kick / 7-metre throw converted.
powerPlaygoal (ice hockey): scored with a man advantage.
shortHandedgoal (ice hockey): scored a man down.
emptyNetgoal (ice hockey): scored into an empty net.
onePointgoal (basketball): a free throw.
twoPointsgoal: basketball 2-point field goal; rugby conversion.
threePointsgoal: basketball 3-pointer; rugby penalty goal or drop goal.
trygoal (rugby): a try.
touchdowngoal (American football): a touchdown.
extraPointgoal (American football): an extra point.
fieldGoalgoal (American football): a field goal.
twoPointConversiongoal (American football): a two-point conversion.
safetygoal (American football): a safety.
yellowcard: yellow card.
secondYellowcard: second yellow, i.e. a sending-off.
redcard: straight red card.
injurysubstitution: forced by an injury.
goalAwardedvarDecision: goal given after review.
goalNotAwardedvarDecision: goal ruled out after review.
penaltyAwardedvarDecision: penalty given after review.
penaltyNotAwardedvarDecision: penalty cancelled after review.
cardUpgradevarDecision: card upgraded (e.g. yellow → red).
cardDowngradevarDecision: card downgraded.
scoredshootoutPenalty: kick scored.
missedshootoutPenalty / inGamePenalty: kick missed or saved (`reason` says which).
twoMinutessuspension: a two-minute (minor) penalty.
fiveMinutessuspension: a five-minute (major) penalty.
tenMinutessuspension: a ten-minute (misconduct) penalty.
otherA kind the source sent that this API does not classify yet.

leftFootLeft foot.
headHeader.
otherAny other body part.

highLeftOn target, high left.

highRightOn target, high right.

rightWide right.

closeHighJust over.

closeHighRightJust over, right.

PointsFormat

tennisTennis: sets → games → points (`sets[].games`).

What a tennis point meant for one side.

wonWon the point, nothing more to mark.
noneNothing to mark for this side — mostly: lost the point (the point that ends a tie-break can be `none` for both).
breakPointAfter this point the side, receiving, has a break point (one point from breaking serve).
setPointAfter this point the side has a set point — a match point too when the set decides the match (the source does not tell them apart). Beats breakPoint and miniBreak.
miniBreakTie-break: won this point on the opponent’s serve.
otherA type not classified yet (the source’s code is logged).

dotNo run.

sixA six.

wideA wide (an extra; the ball is bowled again).
noBallA no-ball (an extra; the ball is bowled again).
legByeLeg byes (extras off the body).
byeByes (extras past the keeper).
otherA delivery not classified yet (the source’s code is logged).

WinProbabilityModel

Model version (the docs describe each). A new version is announced in the changelog.

v1The first model (2026-10-22): pre-match from the current competition’s table and form only. Still served for fixtures whose pre-match estimate was fixed before v2 (it is kept once a match starts).
v2Since 2026-10-22: pre-match from both teams’ recent matches in all competitions, their domestic league tables and our league-strength coefficients (teams of different leagues on one scale), blended with the current competition’s table as it fills up. In play identical to v1. Still served for fixtures whose pre-match estimate was fixed before v3.
v3Since 2026-10-25: v2’s pre-match estimate, except that a league match with a newcomer (one side promoted or relegated into the competition, early in a season) uses the current table and form only, plus the Turkish 1.Lig in the league-strength coefficients; in play, v2’s formula with a calibration step that makes the curve slightly less certain (it was a little over-confident), phased in over the first 15 minutes.

WinProbabilityReason

Why a win-probability point was emitted.

kickoffThe match started: the pre-match estimate at minute 0.
minuteA regular once-a-minute point (time running down moves the estimate even when nothing happens).
goalRight after a goal (own goals count for the side credited).
redCardRight after a red card (a second yellow included).
periodStartA period started: the second half, or a half of extra time.
periodEndA period ended: half-time, the end of regulation, the end of extra time.
bigChanceRight after a big chance that was not scored (a shot of at least 0.3 expected goals) — marks the moment on the curve; the model (v1 and v2 alike) does not blend live expected goals into the estimate.
finalThe match is over: the result, as certainty (1 / 0 / 0).

CommentaryKind

What a commentary entry is about.

kickoffThe match kicked off.
goalA goal (own goals and penalties included).
redCardA sending-off (a straight red or a second yellow).
missedPenaltyA penalty during play that was missed or saved (a scored one is a goal).
varDecisionA video-review decision: goal or penalty given / ruled out, card changed.
bigChanceA big chance that was not scored (a shot of at least 0.3 expected goals).
momentumOne side has had sustained pressure for several minutes (the attack-momentum graph).
periodStartThe second half or a half of extra time started.
periodEndRegulation time or the first half of extra time ended, and play goes on.
halfTimeHalf-time summary.
fullTimeFull-time summary.
updateA summary of the match so far, written when commentary starts during a match.
correctionThe source credited a goal already commented to another player: one line naming the scorer it now gives (earlier entries stay as written). Since 2026-10-27.

PlayByPlayType

What a play-by-play entry records.

matchStartedFootball: a half (or a half of extra time) kicked off.
matchEndedFootball: the match is over.
endFirstHalfFootball: the first half ended.
endSecondHalfFootball: the second half ended.
periodStartBasketball and other clock sports: a period started (the opening tip is a periodStart too).
periodEndBasketball and other clock sports: a period ended.
addedTimeFootball: the fourth official announced added time (the minutes are in `text`).
scoreChangeThe score changed: a goal, or points in basketball (`scoreType` says which); `homeScore` / `awayScore` are the score after it.
shotSavedFootball: a shot on target that was saved.
shotOffTargetA shot that missed: off target (football), a missed field goal (basketball).
shotBlockedFootball: a shot blocked by a defender.
cornerKickFootball: a corner kick (`player` = the defender who conceded it; `side` is his side, so the corner was won by the other one).
freeKickWonFootball: a free kick won (`player` = the player fouled).
freeKickLostFootball: a foul conceded (`player` = the player who fouled).
offsideFootball: a player caught offside.
yellowCardFootball: a yellow card.
redCardFootball: a red card (a second yellow included).
substitutionA substitution (`playerIn` / `playerOut`).
startDelayFootball: play stopped (an injury, a delay).
endDelayFootball: play resumed after a delay.
foulBasketball: a foul (`player` = who fouled, `drawnBy` = who drew it).
freeThrowMissedBasketball: a missed free throw.
reboundBasketball: a rebound (offensive or defensive, see `text`).
possessionChangeBasketball: a turnover (`stolenBy` = the player who stole the ball, when there was a steal).
jumpBallBasketball: a jump ball.
lineupChangeBasketball: a side’s five on the floor changed (the names are in `text`).
timeoutA timeout.
stoppageBasketball: the clock stopped (out of bounds, …).
reviewAn instant-replay review and its outcome (in `text`); in football a VAR decision.
penaltyAwardedFootball: a penalty kick awarded (`player` = the player fouled, `side` = his side).
penaltyConcededFootball: a penalty kick conceded (`player` = the player who gave it away, `side` = his side).
penaltyScoredFootball: a goal from a penalty kick in play. `homeScore` / `awayScore` = the score after it, counted on from the previous goal of the list (the source gives none on this entry); null in a penalty shoot-out, which does not change the match score.
penaltyMissedFootball: a penalty kick missed (off target).
penaltySavedFootball: a penalty kick saved by the goalkeeper.
violationBasketball: a violation (kicked ball, goaltending, …; the kind is in `text`).
otherAnother kind of entry (a value the source added later — read `text`).

StandingsSource

Where a standings table comes from — `meta.source` of /standings.

upstreamThe table as the data source publishes it.

SeriesFiguresSource

Where a series table’s wins / podiums / polePositions / racesStarted / racesWithPoints come from — `meta.figuresSource` of /series/{id}/standings.

upstreamAs the data source publishes them (null where it has none).
computedComputed by us from the main race of every finished championship round, because the source publishes only positions and points (MotoGP): wins = 1st, podiums = top 3, polePositions = started from grid position 1, racesStarted = races started (a team: races with at least one entry started), racesWithPoints = races that scored points; a team counts every entry. Sprints are not counted. fastestLaps stays null when the races do not report them.

WsErrorCode

WebSocket error code.

bad_frameThe frame was not valid JSON, not a known shape, or lacks a field it needs (`message` names the field, e.g. "channel: required").
unknown_channelNot a channel name we serve (or an unknown sport slug).
channel_forbiddenThe channel is not in your plan’s grade.
unknown_leagueleague:{id} names a league id we never issued (use the ids of /v2/leagues and of fixtures’ league) — REST answers the same id with 404 not_found.
unknown_fixturefixture:{id} names a fixture id we never issued — REST answers the same id with 404 not_found. The channel is not counted.
unknown_racerace:{id} names no race (a season or session id, or one we never issued) — /v2/races/{id} answers the same id with 404. The channel is not counted.
not_subscribedresync / unsubscribe of a channel this connection is not on.
too_many_channelsYou hit maxChannels on this connection.
snapshot_failedThe snapshot could not be built — send resync to retry (for league:{id}, when the league id could not be checked right now: subscribe again).
rate_limitedMore than 60 frames in 10 seconds on this connection; frames are dropped until the window resets.
